title.zh: 卷十四 志第四 地理上
title.raw: 卷十四 志第四 地理上 Volume 14 Treatises 4: Geography Part One

sentences.zh: 昔者元胎無象，太素流形，對越在天，以爲元首，則記所謂冬居營窟，夏居橧巢，飲血茹毛，未有麻絲者也。

translations.literal: In antiquity the primordial embryo had no image; Grand Simplicity flowed into forms; facing and answering what is on high, they took it as the supreme head—then the records say they dwelt in burrows in winter and nests in summer, drank blood and ate fur, and had not yet hemp or silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the earliest age, before form coalesced from undivided simplicity, people already looked toward heaven as their sovereign; the old annals picture them wintering in earthen dens, summering in treetop huts, living on raw flesh and blood, long before cloth ever softened their lives.

sentences.zh: 及燧人鑽火，庖犧出震，風宗下武，炎胤昌基，畫野無聞，其歸一揆。

translations.literal: When Suiren drilled fire, Paoxi emerged in the Zhen (east) trigram; wind took lineage and descended to Wu; blazing heirs broadened the foundation; dividing the wilds is not heard of—their return is one measure.
translations.idiomatic: Then Suiren struck fire from wood, Fuxi rose in the east like thunder, wind and flame passed their line down to martial kings, and the royal house widened its base; we hear nothing yet of surveying fields into squares, but every step still aimed at the same single standard of rule.

sentences.zh: 黃帝則東海南江，登空躡岱，至於崑峰振轡，崆山訪道，[1]存諸汗竹，不可厚誣。

translations.literal: As for the Yellow Emperor: east to the sea, south to the great rivers; ascending hollow (Kong) and treading Dai; reaching Kun peaks to shake the reins, Kongshan to inquire of the Way—[1] it is preserved on sweating bamboo strips and cannot be heavily slandered.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor pressed east to the sea and south along the great streams, climbed Kongsang and crossed Mount Tai, climbed Kunlun to tighten his reins and sought the Way on Kongshan; the fact is inked on bamboo that has soaked in human sweat, and it would be perverse to dismiss it as mere legend.

sentences.zh: 高陽任地依神，帝嚳順天行義。

translations.literal: Gaoyang relied on earth and depended on spirits; Emperor Ku followed heaven and practiced righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanxu, the High Yang line, grounded his power in the land and the spirits; Emperor Ku shaped policy by heaven's pattern and the moral law.

sentences.zh: 東踰蟠木，西濟流沙，北至幽陵，南撫交阯，日月所經，舟車所至，莫匪王臣，不踰茲域。

translations.literal: East they crossed Panmu, west they forded the flowing sands, north they reached Youling, south they soothed Jiaozhi; wherever sun and moon passed, wherever boat and cart could reach, none were not the king's subjects—they did not overstep this domain.
translations.idiomatic: Their sway ran east past the curling forest, west across the shifting sands, north to the cold marches, south to the Red River delta—every place the sun and moon lit and every road a wheel could find lay inside the ring of royal subjects, and nothing beyond that ring counted as theirs.

sentences.zh: 帝堯時，禹平水土，以爲九州。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Yao, Yu pacified the waters and earth, and thereby made the nine provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yao, Yu drained the flood and settled the soil, and from that labor the Nine Provinces took their shape.

sentences.zh: 虞舜登庸，厥功彌劭，表提類而分區宇，判山河而考疆域，冀北創并部之名，燕齊起幽營之號，則書所謂肇十有二州，封十有二山者也。

translations.literal: When Shun of Yu ascended to employment, his merit grew ever greater; he displayed categories and divided the regional cosmos, adjudicated mountains and rivers and examined boundaries; north of Ji he created the name of the Bing department; in Yan and Qi he raised the designations of You and Ying—this is what the documents call initiating twelve provinces and enfeoffing twelve mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shun took office, his achievement only deepened: he sorted kinds of terrain, carved the realm into regions, traced ranges and rivers to fix true borders, split the northern Ji plain to name the Bing command, and gave Yan and Qi the new titles of You and Ying—exactly the twelve provinces and twelve sacred peaks the classics say he first ordained.

sentences.zh: 夏功在于唐堯，殷因無所損益。

translations.literal: The Xia's achievement lay in Tang-Yao; the Yin inherited and had nothing to diminish or increase.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia built on the work of Yao of Tang; the Shang inherited that map and left its proportions unchanged.

translations.literal: King Wu of Zhou conquered Shang, from Feng going to Hao.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu of Zhou overthrew the Shang, he moved the seat of power from Feng to Hao.

sentences.zh: 至成王時，改作禹貢，徐梁入於青雍，冀野析於幽并。

translations.literal: By the time of King Cheng, they revised and made the Tribute of Yu; Xu and Liang were absorbed into Qing and Yong; the wilds of Ji were split into You and Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Under King Cheng the court rewrote the "Tribute of Yu" grid: Xu and Liang were folded into Qing and Yong, while the old Ji heartland was carved into new You and Bing sectors.

sentences.zh: 職方掌天下之土，以周厥利；

translations.literal: The Office of Regions grasped the soil of all under heaven, in order to complete its advantages;
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Domains held the register of every soil under heaven, weighing what each tract could yield;

sentences.zh: 保章辯九州之野，皆有分星。

translations.literal: The Star-Clerk distinguished the wilds of the nine provinces; each had apportioned stars.
translations.idiomatic: The star-masters matched each of the Nine Provinces to its own stretch of sky, every region with its allotted constellation.

sentences.zh: 東南曰揚州，正南曰荊州，河南曰豫州，正東曰青州，河東曰兗州，正西曰雍州，東北曰幽州，河內曰冀州，正北曰并州。

translations.literal: The southeast is called Yangzhou, the due south Jingzhou, south of the river Yuzhou, the due east Qingzhou, east of the river Yanzhou, the due west Yongzhou, the northeast Youzhou, within the river Jizhou, the due north Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The southeast quarter was Yangzhou, the south face Jingzhou, the ground south of the Yellow River Yuzhou, the east face Qingzhou, the ground east of the river Yanzhou, the west face Yongzhou, the northeast Youzhou, the inner bend of the river Jizhou, and the north face Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 始皇初并天下，懲{乂心}戰國，削罷列侯，分天下爲三十六郡。

translations.literal: When the First Emperor first united all under heaven, chastened by the Warring States, he cut away and abolished the ranked feudal lords and divided all under heaven into thirty-six commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor, fresh from unifying the realm and determined not to repeat Warring States chaos, stripped the old enfeoffed nobles of power and carved the empire into thirty-six commanderies.

sentences.zh: 〈三川、河東、南陽、南郡、九江、鄣郡、會稽、潁川、碭郡、泗水、薛郡、東郡、琅邪、齊郡、上谷、漁陽、右北平、遼西、遼東、代郡、鉅鹿、邯鄲、上黨、太原、雲中、九原、雁門、上郡、隴西、北地、漢中、巴郡、蜀郡、黔中、長沙，凡三十五郡，與內史爲三十六郡也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Sanchuan, Hedong, Nanyang, Nanjun, Jiujiang, Zhang commandery, Kuaiji, Yingchuan, Dang commandery, Sishui, Xue commandery, Dong commandery, Langye, Qi commandery, Shanggu, Yuyang, Right Beiping, Liaoxi, Liaodong, Dai commandery, Julu, Handan, Shangdang, Taiyuan, Yunzhong, Jiuyuan, Yanmen, Shang commandery, Longxi, Beidi, Hanzhong, Ba commandery, Shu commandery, Qianzhong, Changsha—in all thirty-five commanderies, which together with the metropolitan intendant made thirty-six commanderies.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The gloss lists thirty-five outer commanderies—from Sanchuan and Hedong down the coast to Changsha—and counts them with the capital intendant's district to make the famous thirty-six.〉

sentences.zh: 於是興師踰江，平取百越，又置閩中、南海、桂林、象郡，凡四十郡，郡一守焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon they raised armies and crossed the rivers, pacified and took the Hundred Yue, and further established Minzhong, Nanhai, Guilin, and Xiang commanderies—in all forty commanderies, each commandery having one governor.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent armies south of the Yangtze, crushed the Yue peoples, and added Minzhong, Nanhai, Guilin, and Xiang, bringing the whole system to forty commanderies, each overseen by a single appointed governor.

sentences.zh: 其地則西臨洮而北沙漠，東縈西帶，皆臨大海。

translations.literal: As for the territory: west it bordered Tao and north the desert; east winding, west belting—all bordered the great sea.
translations.idiomatic: The new realm ran west to the Tao River and north to the sands, while east and south it looped like a sash until every outer edge touched the sea.

sentences.zh: 漢祖龍興，革秦之弊，分內史爲三部，更置郡國二十有三，

translations.literal: The Han progenitor rose like a dragon, reformed the Qin's abuses, divided the metropolitan intendant into three parts, and further established twenty-three commanderies and kingdoms,
translations.idiomatic: When the Han founder seized the mandate, he undid Qin's excesses, split the old inner intendant into three metropolitan circuits, and added twenty-three new commanderies and princely kingdoms,

sentences.zh: 〈桂陽、江夏、豫章、河內、魏郡、東海、楚國、平原、梁國、定襄、泰山、汝南、淮陽、千乘、東萊、燕國、清河、信都、常山、中山、渤海、廣漢、涿郡，合二十三也。

translations.literal: 〈Guiyang, Jiangxia, Yuzhang, Henei, Wei commandery, Donghai, Chu kingdom, Pingyuan, Liang kingdom, Dingxiang, Taishan, Runan, Huaiyang, Qiansheng, Donglai, Yan kingdom, Qinghe, Xindu, Changshan, Zhongshan, Bohai, Guanghan, Zhuo commandery—together twenty-three.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈namely Guiyang through Zhuo commandery, twenty-three units in all.〉

sentences.zh: 三內史者，河上、渭南、中地也。

translations.literal: The three metropolitan intendants are: Heshang, Weinan, and Zhongdi.
translations.idiomatic: The three inner districts were Heshang south of the bend, Weinan, and the central capital belt.

sentences.zh: 地理志曰：高祖增二十六，武帝改河上、渭南、中地以爲京兆、馮翊、扶風，是爲三輔也。〉

translations.literal: The Treatise on Geography says: Gaozu added twenty-six; Emperor Wu changed Heshang, Weinan, and Zhongdi into Jingzhao, Fengyi, and Fufeng—this is the Three Adjuncts.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Han geography adds that Gaozu created twenty-six units and that Emperor Wu renamed the three inner belts Jingzhao, Fengyi, and Fufeng—the region later called the Three Adjuncts of Chang'an.〉

translations.literal: Wen added thereto nine,
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han added nine more,

sentences.zh: 〈廣平、城陽、淄川、濟南、膠西、膠東、河間、廬江、衡山，武帝改衡山曰「六安」。〉

translations.literal: 〈Guangping, Chengyang, Zichuan, Jinan, Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Hejian, Lujiang, Hengshan—Emperor Wu changed Hengshan to "Liu'an."〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Guangping, Chengyang, Zichuan, Jinan, Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Hejian, Lujiang, and Hengshan—the last of which Emperor Wu renamed Liu'an.〉

translations.literal: Jing added four of them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing added four more.

translations.literal: 〈Jibei, Jiyin, Shanyang, and Beihai.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Jibei, Jiyin, Shanyang, and Beihai.〉

translations.literal: Xuan changed Jibei to Dongping.〉
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan renamed Jibei as Dongping.〉

sentences.zh: 武帝開越攘胡，初置十七，

translations.literal: Emperor Wu opened the Yue and pushed back the Hu, at first establishing seventeen,
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu campaigned south against Yue and north against the steppe peoples, and his first expansion added seventeen commanderies,

sentences.zh: 〈南海、蒼梧、鬱林、合浦、交阯、九真、日南、珠崖、儋耳九郡，平西南夷置牂柯、越巂、沈黎、汶山、犍爲、益州六郡，西置武都郡，又分立零陵郡，合十七郡。〉

translations.literal: 〈Nanhai, Cangwu, Yulin, Hepu, Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen, Rinan, Zhuya, Dan'er—nine commanderies; pacifying the southwestern Yi, established Zangke, Yuexi, Chenli, Wenshan, Qianwei, Yizhou—six commanderies; west established Wudu commandery; again separately established Lingling commandery—together seventeen commanderies.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈nine southern coast commands from Nanhai to Dan'er, six carved from the southwest Yi heartland, Wudu on the western flank, and a split Lingling—seventeen new units in that push.〉

translations.literal: Expanding soil and dividing boundaries, again added fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: Further conquests widened the map by fourteen more commanderies.

sentences.zh: 〈弘農、臨淮、西河、朔方、酒泉、陳留、安定、天水、玄菟、樂浪、廣陵、敦煌、武威、張掖。〉

translations.literal: 〈Hongnong, Linhuai, Xihe, Shuofang, Jiuquan, Chenliu, Anding, Tianshui, Xuantu, Lelang, Guangling, Dunhuang, Wuwei, Zhangye.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Hongnong through Zhangye—the fourteen interior and frontier seats listed in the commentary.〉

translations.literal: Emperor Zhao had few undertakings, again added one thereof.
translations.idiomatic: Under the short reign of Emperor Zhao the court added only one more.

translations.literal: 〈Jincheng.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Jincheng commandery.〉

sentences.zh: 至平帝元始二年，凡新置郡國七十有一，與秦四十，合一百一十有一。

translations.literal: Down to Emperor Ping's Yuanshi second year, in all newly established commanderies and kingdoms were seventy-one; together with Qin's forty, altogether one hundred eleven.
translations.idiomatic: By the second year of Yuanshi under Emperor Ping, Han had founded seventy-one new units; added to Qin's forty, the roster stood at one hundred eleven.

sentences.zh: 改雍曰涼，改梁曰益，又置徐州，復夏舊號，南置交阯，北有朔方，凡爲十三部。

translations.literal: Changed Yong to Liang, changed Liang to Yi, further established Xuzhou, restored Xia's old designations, south established Jiaozhi, north had Shuofang—in all became thirteen departments.
translations.idiomatic: Yong became Liang, Liang became Yi, Xuzhou returned to the rolls, southern Jiaozhi and northern Shuofang were wired in, and the old Xia-style names were revived until the realm sat in thirteen inspectorates.

sentences.zh: 〈涼、益、荊、揚、青、豫、兗、徐、幽、并、冀十一州，交阯、朔方二刺史，合十三部。〉

translations.literal: 〈Liang, Yi, Jing, Yang, Qing, Yu, Yan, Xu, You, Bing, Ji—eleven provinces; Jiaozhi, Shuofang—two regional inspectors; together thirteen departments.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Eleven provinces from Liang to Ji plus two special zones, Jiaozhi and Shuofang, each with its own regional commissioner—thirteen departments in all.〉

sentences.zh: 光武投戈之歲，在彫秏之辰，郡國蕭條，并省者八。

translations.literal: In the year Guangwu cast aside the spear, it was a time of wasting exhaustion; commanderies and kingdoms were desolate; those merged and abolished were eight.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangwu laid down the sword, the realm was gaunt from war; eight redundant commanderies were folded away in the general retrenchment.

sentences.zh: 〈城陽、淄川、高密、膠東、六安、真定、泗水、廣陽。〉

translations.literal: 〈Chengyang, Zichuan, Gaomi, Jiaodong, Liu'an, Zhending, Sishui, Guangyang.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Chengyang, Zichuan, Gaomi, Jiaodong, Liu'an, Zhending, Sishui, and Guangyang were the eight struck from the map.〉

sentences.zh: 建武十一年，省州牧，復爲刺史，員十三人，各掌一州。

translations.literal: Jianwu eleventh year, abolished provincial shepherds, again became censors; establishment thirteen men, each grasping one province.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Jianwu the court abolished the provincial governorships, restored classic regional censors, and fixed their number at thirteen, one to each major province.

translations.literal: Mingdi established one,
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming added one seat,

translations.literal: 〈Yongchang.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Yongchang in the far southwest.〉

translations.literal: Zhangdi established two,
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhang added two commands,

translations.literal: 〈Rencheng, Wu commandery.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Rencheng and Wu commandery.〉

translations.literal: He and Shun altered and made; their names were nine.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors He and Shun the map was redrawn nine times.

sentences.zh: 〈和置濟北、廣陽，順改淮陽爲陳，改楚爲彭城，濟東爲東平，臨淮爲下邳，千乘爲六安，信都爲安平，天水爲漢陽。〉

translations.literal: 〈He established Jibei and Guangyang; Shun changed Huaiyang to Chen, changed Chu to Pengcheng, Jidong to Dongping, Linhuai to Xiapi, Qiansheng to Liu'an, Xindu to Anping, Tianshui to Hanyang.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emperor He revived Jibei and Guangyang; Emperor Shun renamed Huaiyang as Chen, the old Chu core as Pengcheng, Jidong as Dongping, Linhuai as Xiapi, Qiansheng as Liu'an, Xindu as Anping, and Tianshui as Hanyang.〉

sentences.zh: 省朔方刺史，合之於司隸，凡十三部，

translations.literal: Abolished the Shuofang regional inspector, merged it into the Metropolitan Superintendent; in all thirteen departments,
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang's inspectorate was folded into the capital superintendent's zone, leaving thirteen departments in the Eastern Han scheme,

sentences.zh: 〈其與西漢不同者，司隸校尉部郡治河南，朔方隸於并部。〉

translations.literal: 〈Where it differs from Western Han: the Metropolitan Superintendent's commandery-administered region takes Henan as its seat; Shuofang is subordinate to Bing department.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Unlike Western Han, the metropolitan belt was administered from Henan, while Shuofang answered to the Bing inspector rather than standing alone.〉

translations.literal: And commanderies and kingdoms were one hundred eight.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Han roster thus held one hundred eight commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 〈省前漢八，分置五，改舊名七，因舊九十六，少前漢三也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Abolished eight of Former Han, split and established five, changed old names seven, continued old ninety-six—three fewer than Former Han.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Eight Western Han units were cut, five new ones split off, seven were simply renamed, ninety-six kept their old titles—three fewer than the old Han total.〉

sentences.zh: 桓靈頗增於前，復置六郡。

translations.literal: Huan and Ling somewhat increased over before, again established six commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Huan and Ling the court added six commanderies beyond the earlier baseline.

translations.literal: 〈Huan: Gaoyang, Gaoliang, Boling;
translations.idiomatic: 〈Emperor Huan created Gaoyang, Gaoliang, and Boling;

translations.literal: Ling: Nan'an, Poyang, Luling.〉
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling added Nan'an, Poyang, and Luling.〉

sentences.zh: 魏武定霸，三方鼎立，生靈版蕩，關洛荒蕪，所置者十二，

translations.literal: Wei Wu settled hegemony; the three sides stood like a tripod; living beings were on tablet-like upheaval; Guan and Luo were desolate; those established were twelve,
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao seized the north the realm split three ways, the people were scattered like tablets on a flood, the old capitals lay in ruins, and he could found only twelve new commanderies,

sentences.zh: 〈新興、樂平、西平、新平、略陽、陰平、帶方、譙、樂陵、章武、南鄉、襄陽。〉

translations.literal: 〈Xinxing, Leping, Xiping, Xinping, Lueyang, Yinping, Daifang, Qiao, Leling, Zhangwu, Nanxiang, Xiangyang.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈from Xinxing down the Han river arc to Xiangyang, twelve seats in all.〉

translations.literal: Those abolished were seven,
translations.idiomatic: Seven older commands were struck at the same time,

sentences.zh: 〈上郡、朔方、五原、雲中、定襄、漁陽、廬江。〉

translations.literal: 〈Shang commandery, Shuofang, Wuyuan, Yunzhong, Dingxiang, Yuyang, Lujiang.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Shang, Shuofang, Wuyuan, Yunzhong, Dingxiang, Yuyang, and Lujiang were the seven removed.〉

translations.literal: And Wendi established seven,
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei then added seven more,

sentences.zh: 〈朝歌、陽平、弋陽、魏興、新城、義陽、[2]安豐。〉

translations.literal: 〈Zhaoge, Yangping, Yiyang (弋陽), Weixing, Xincheng, Yiyang (義陽), [2] Anfeng.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Zhaoge, Yangping, the Ru-nan Yiyang, Weixing, Xincheng, the Huai-line Yiyang, and Anfeng.〉

translations.literal: Ming and the Lesser Emperor added two,
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming and the first boy emperor each added one commandery—two in all,

translations.literal: 〈Ming: Shangyong;
translations.idiomatic: 〈Mingdi restored Shangyong;

translations.literal: Lesser: Pingyang.〉
translations.idiomatic: the boy emperor added Pingyang.〉

translations.literal: Those obtaining Han commanderies were fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Wei thus held fifty-four commanderies inherited from Han.

sentences.zh: 蜀先主於漢建安之間初置郡九，

translations.literal: Shu's First Sovereign, in the interval of Han's Jian'an, first established nine commanderies,
translations.idiomatic: Between the Jian'an years, Liu Bei in Shu-Han first carved out nine commanderies,

sentences.zh: 〈巴東、巴西、梓潼、江陽、汶山、漢嘉、朱提、宕渠、涪陵。〉

translations.literal: 〈Badong, Baxi, Zitong, Jiangyang, Wenshan, Hanjia, Zhuti, Dangqu, Fuling.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Badong, Baxi, Zitong, Jiangyang, Wenshan, Hanjia, Zhuti, Dangqu, and Fuling.〉

translations.literal: The Later Sovereign added two,
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan later added two more,

translations.literal: 〈Yunnan, Xingu.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Yunnan and Xingu in the far south.〉

translations.literal: Those obtaining Han commanderies were eleven.
translations.idiomatic: Shu ultimately held eleven Han-era commanderies.

translations.literal: The Wu ruler, the Great Emperor, first established five commanderies,
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan, Wu's Great Emperor, first founded five commanderies,

sentences.zh: 〈臨賀、武昌、珠崖、新安、廬陵南部。〉

translations.literal: 〈Linhe, Wuchang, Zhuya, Xin'an, southern Luling.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Linhe, Wuchang, Zhuya, Xin'an, and the southern annex of Luling.〉

translations.literal: The Lesser Emperor and Emperor Jing each four,
translations.idiomatic: Sun Liang and Sun Xiu each added four commanderies,

translations.literal: 〈Lesser: Linchuan, Linhai, Hengyang, Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Sun Liang created Linchuan, Linhai, Hengyang, and Xiangdong;

sentences.zh: 景，天門、建安、建平、合浦北部。〉

translations.literal: Jing: Tianmen, Jian'an, Jianping, northern Hepu.〉
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu added Tianmen, Jian'an, Jianping, and northern Hepu.〉

translations.literal: The Marquis Who Submits to Fate also established twelve commanderies,
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao, the "Marquis Who Surrendered His Mandate," still ordered twelve more commanderies founded,

sentences.zh: 〈始安、始興、邵陵、安成、新昌、武平、九德、吳興、東陽、桂林、滎陽、宜都。〉

translations.literal: 〈Shi'an, Shixing, Shaoling, Ancheng, Xinchang, Wuping, Jiude, Wuxing, Dongyang, Guilin, Yingyang, Yidu.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Shi'an, Shixing, Shaoling, Ancheng, Xinchang, Wuping, Jiude, Wuxing, Dongyang, Guilin, Yingyang, and Yidu.〉

translations.literal: Those obtaining Han commanderies were eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: Wu in the end controlled eighteen commanderies that had once belonged to Han.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康元年，既平孫氏，凡增置郡國二十有三，

translations.literal: Jin Emperor Wu, Taikang first year, having already pacified the Sun clan, in all added twenty-three commanderies and kingdoms,
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taikang, after Jin Wudi crushed the Sun regime, the court created twenty-three new commanderies and kingdoms,

sentences.zh: 〈滎陽、上洛、頓丘、臨淮、東莞、襄城、汝陰、長廣、廣甯、昌黎、新野、隨郡、陰平、義陽、毗陵、宣城、南康、晉安、寧浦、始平、略陽、樂平、南平。〉

translations.literal: 〈Yingyang, Shangluo, Dunqiu, Linhuai, Dongguan, Xiangcheng, Ru'yin, Changguang, Guangning, Changli, Xinye, Sui commandery, Yinping, Yiyang, Piling, Xuancheng, Nankang, Jin'an, Ningpu, Shiping, Lueyang, Leping, Nanping.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Twenty-three units from Yingyang on the Yellow River plain to Nanping on the southern rim.〉

sentences.zh: 省司隸置司州，別立梁、秦、寧、平四州，仍吳之廣州，凡十九州，

translations.literal: Abolished the Metropolitan Superintendent and established Sizhou; separately established Liang, Qin, Ning, and Ping four provinces; continued Wu's Guangzhou—in all nineteen provinces,
translations.idiomatic: The old metropolitan belt became Sizhou, Liang, Qin, Ning, and Ping were spun off as new provinces, Wu's Guangzhou was kept, and the empire was reorganized into nineteen provinces,

sentences.zh: 〈司、冀、兗、豫、荊、徐、揚、青、幽、平、并、雍、涼、秦、梁、益、寧、交、廣州。〉

translations.literal: 〈Si, Ji, Yan, Yu, Jing, Xu, Yang, Qing, You, Ping, Bing, Yong, Liang (Hexi), Qin, Liang (Hanzhong), Yi, Ning, Jiao, Guang provinces.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Si through Guang—the nineteen names that now girdled the reunited realm.〉

translations.literal: Commanderies and kingdoms one hundred seventy-three,
translations.idiomatic: The commandery and kingdom count stood at one hundred seventy-three,

sentences.zh: 〈仍吳所置二十五，仍蜀新置十一，仍魏所置二十一，仍漢舊九十三，置二十三。〉

translations.literal: 〈Continued twenty-five set by Wu, continued eleven newly set by Shu, continued twenty-one set by Wei, continued ninety-three old Han ones, established twenty-three.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Twenty-five Wu foundations, eleven Shu additions, twenty-one Wei creations, ninety-three Han survivals, and twenty-three brand-new Jin seats.〉

sentences.zh: 以爲冠帶之國，盡有殷周之土。

translations.literal: Thereby making the cap-and-belt states; fully possessing the soil of Yin and Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin now wore the full cap-and-girdle dignity of the central states and held every tract the Yin and Zhou kings had once claimed.

sentences.zh: 若乃敦龐於天地之始，昭晰於犧農之世，用長黎元，未爭疆埸。

translations.literal: As for being rich and vast at heaven and earth's beginning, bright and clear in the age of Xi and Shennong, thereby lengthening the black-haired people—not yet contending over border fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the first mists of creation life spread in generous abundance; under Fuxi and Shennong the world grew plain and bright, and the people multiplied long before anyone quarreled over furrows on a map.

sentences.zh: 而玉環楛矢，夷裘風駕，南翬表貺，東風入律，光乎上德，奚遠弗臻。

translations.literal: Moreover jade rings and blunt-arrow tribute, Yi furs and wind-borne carriages, southern pheasant-plumes displaying gifts, east wind entering the pitch-pipes—shining with high virtue, what distant place did not arrive?
translations.idiomatic: Jade rings and blunt arrows, furs from forest peoples, embassies riding the seasonal winds, southern birds offered as tribute, eastern breezes tuning the pitch-pipes—all of it proclaimed a sovereign virtue so luminous that no corner of the map stayed beyond reach.

sentences.zh: 然則星象麗天，山河紀地，端掖裁其弘敞，崤函判其都邑，仰觀俯察，萬物攸歸。

translations.literal: Thus then star-patterns attach to heaven, mountains and rivers record earth; the layered palace avenues bound their vast breadth, the Xiao and Han passes mark their capitals; looking up, looking down, the myriad things have their return.
translations.idiomatic: Stars lace the sky while mountains and rivers score the earth; palace avenues pace out the capital's grandeur, the Xiao and Han passes mark where dynasties chose to sit—look up or down and every creature finds its place inside that frame.

sentences.zh: 是以洛沚咸陽，宛然秦漢，晉濱河西，同知堯禹，于茲新邑，宅是鎬京，五尺童子皆能口誦者，史官弗之書也。

translations.literal: Therefore Luozhi and Xianyang, just so Qin and Han; Jin along the west of the river, likewise knowing Yao and Yu; at this new city, dwelling is Haojing—what even a five-foot child can recite from memory, the historiographers do not write thereof.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone nods when you name the Luo shoals or Xianyang as the heart of Qin and Han, or liken Jin's hold on the western riverbank to the world Yao and Shun knew; every schoolchild can chant how the new capital sits where Haojing once stood—truths so worn smooth by memory that the official annals pass them by in silence.

sentences.zh: 昔庖犧氏生於成紀，而爲天子，都於陳。

translations.literal: Formerly Paoxi was born at Chenji and became Son of Heaven, with capital at Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Legend places Fuxi's birth at Chenji and his enthronement at Chen.

sentences.zh: 神農氏都陳，而別營于曲阜。

translations.literal: Shennong took Chen as capital, but separately encamped at Qufu.
translations.idiomatic: Shennong ruled from Chen yet pitched a second court at Qufu.

sentences.zh: 黃帝生於壽丘，而都於涿鹿。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor was born at Shouqiu, but had capital at Zhuolu.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor was born on Shouqiu hill and built his capital at Zhuolu.

sentences.zh: 少昊始自窮桑，而遷都曲阜。

translations.literal: Shaohao began from Qiongsang, but moved the capital to Qufu.
translations.idiomatic: Shaohao rose from Qiongsang and later shifted his seat to Qufu.

sentences.zh: 顓頊始自窮桑，而徙邑商丘。

translations.literal: Zhuanxu began from Qiongsang, but moved the town to Shangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanxu likewise started from Qiongsang before relocating his capital to Shangqiu.

translations.literal: Gaoxin assumed the title, established capital at Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoxin took the throne-name and founded his capital at Bo.

sentences.zh: 孫卿子曰：「不登高山，不知天之高；

translations.literal: Master Xun Qing said: "If you do not climb a high mountain, you do not know heaven's height;
translations.idiomatic: Xunzi wrote, "Unless you climb a high peak you cannot grasp how high the sky hangs;"

sentences.zh: 不臨深谿，不知地之厚也。

translations.literal: if you do not overlook a deep ravine, you do not know earth's thickness."
translations.idiomatic: unless you stand above a deep gorge you cannot feel how thick the earth runs beneath you."

sentences.zh: 」大哉坤象，萬物資生，載崑華而不墜，傾河海而寧泄。

translations.literal: "Great is the kun trigram's image; the myriad things rely on it for life; it bears Kunlun and Mount Hua without falling; it tilts the rivers and seas yet is calm in draining."
translations.idiomatic: "Vast is the earth's emblem in the Changes: every creature draws life from it; it shoulders Kunlun and Mount Hua without collapsing, and even when the Yellow River and the sea pour through it, the land does not burst."

sentences.zh: 考卜惟王，乘飛駐軫，睨𡹮山而鐫勒，覽曾城以爲玩。

translations.literal: Divining tortoise-shells for the king, riding flight halting at the axle-ends, gazing askance at Min mountains and carving inscriptions, viewing layered towers as playthings.
translations.idiomatic: Kings read the tortoise cracks, raced chariots to the ends of the roads, squinted up at Minshan and carved boastful stelae, and treated terraced capitals as baubles.

sentences.zh: 時逢稽浸，道接陵夷，平王東遷，星離豆剖，當塗馭宇，瓜分鼎立。

translations.literal: Times encountered famine-floods; the Way met decline; King Ping moved east; stars scattered, beans split; the cart-track clan grasped the cosmos; melons divided, tripod stood apart.
translations.idiomatic: Then came years of flood and dearth, the royal Way slid downhill, Pingwang fled east and the realm shattered like stars and pods, the Caos seized the chariot-reins, and the land was carved into three rival stoves.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝接千祀之餘，當八堯之禪，先王桑梓，罄宇來歸，斯固可得而言者矣。

translations.literal: Shizu Emperor Wu took up the remainder after a thousand sacrifices, faced the abdication like the eight Yao transfers; the Former Kings' mulberry and catalpa— the whole realm came to return—this indeed can be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: Our martial founding emperor, Shizu, picked up the threads after a thousand years of sacrifice, stood in the moment of a mandate-shift worthy of Yao's age, and watched the old heartland—the mulberry-and-catalpa home of the kings—empty itself back into his hands; that much, at least, can be told aloud.

sentences.zh: 惠皇不虞，中州盡棄，永嘉南度，綸行建鄴，九分天下而有二焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui met unexpected disaster; the central plain was wholly abandoned; Yongjia southward crossing, by edict-progress establishing Jiankang; of nine parts of all under heaven they had two.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui fell to calamity the Central Plain was lost; after the Yongjia flight south the court set its capital at Jiankang by imperial decree, holding barely two shares of a realm once counted in ninths.

sentences.zh: 昔大禹觀於濁河而受綠字，寰瀛之內可得而言也。

translations.literal: Formerly Great Yu gazed on the muddy Yellow River and received the green characters; within the ring of the seas it can be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Yu the Great stood by the silty Yellow River and read the green script that mapped the world; inside the belt of the oceans every place can finally be named.

translations.literal: Heaven has seven stars; earth has seven markers;
translations.idiomatic: Seven stellar mansions hang above, and seven terrestrial markers answer them below;

translations.literal: Heaven has four sustaining cords (weft/bindings); earth has four great draining channels.
translations.idiomatic: The sky is hung on four cosmic stays, and the land is gouged by four mighty watercourses that carry the flood away.

translations.literal: Outside the eight cords of the world, they are called the eight extremities.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the encircling girdle that ropes in the known world lie the eight outermost reaches.

sentences.zh: 地不足東南，天不足西北。

translations.literal: Earth falls short toward the southeast; heaven falls short toward the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: The ground gives way to the southeast, while the empyrean gapes widest toward the northwest.

sentences.zh: 八極之廣，東西二億三萬一千三百里，南北二億三萬一千三百里。

translations.literal: The breadth of the eight extremities: east and west, two hundred thirty-one thousand three hundred li; north and south, likewise two hundred thirty-one thousand three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: From the eastern pole to the western spans two hundred thirty-one thousand three hundred li—and the same measure runs from south to north.

sentences.zh: 自地至天，半八極之數，自下亦如之。

translations.literal: From earth to heaven is half the tally of the eight extremities; from below upward it is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The vault above measured half the span of the Eight Poles, and the same depth echoed below.

sentences.zh: 昔黃帝令豎亥步自東極，至于西極，五億十萬九千八百八步。

translations.literal: Formerly the Yellow Emperor ordered Shu Hai to pace from the eastern extremity to the western extremity: five hundred nine thousand eight hundred eight paces.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Yellow Emperor bade Shu Hai stride from sunrise to sunset; the tally came to five hundred nine thousand eight hundred eight measured paces.

sentences.zh: 史臣案，凡周天積百七萬九百一十三里，徑三十五萬六千九百七十里。

translations.literal: The court historiographers ascertain: in all the circumference of heaven totals one million seventy thousand nine hundred thirteen li; the diameter is three hundred fifty-six thousand nine hundred seventy li.
translations.idiomatic: Court mathematicians reckoned heaven's circuit at 1,070,913 li and its diameter at 356,970 li.

sentences.zh: 所謂南北爲經，東西爲緯。

translations.literal: That which is called: north-south as warp, east-west as weft.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by naming north-south the warp and east-west the weft.

sentences.zh: 天有十二次，日月之所躔；

translations.literal: Heaven has twelve celestial lodges; they are where the sun and moon tread their circuits;
translations.idiomatic: Twelve lunar lodges score the sky—the highway of sun and moon;

sentences.zh: 地有十二辰，王侯之所國也。

translations.literal: earth has twelve earthly branches; they are where kings and marquises establish states.
translations.idiomatic: twelve earthly divisions underpin the map where lords and princes plant their altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 或因生得姓，因功命土，祁、酉、燕、齊，在乎茲域。

translations.literal: Some by birth obtain surnames, by merit receive land; Qi, You, Yan, and Qi lie within this region.
translations.idiomatic: Some clans took names from ancestral seats, others earned fiefs for deeds done—and the old domains of Qi, You, Yan, and Qi all fall inside these bounds.

sentences.zh: 昔黃帝旁行天下，方制萬里，得百里之國萬區，則《周易》所謂「首出庶物，萬國咸寧」者也。

translations.literal: Formerly the Yellow Emperor traveled the realm in all directions, regulated a square of ten thousand li, and obtained ten thousand regions of hundred-li states—this is what the Zhou Yi calls "first emerging among the myriad things; the myriad states all attain tranquility."
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Yellow Emperor quartered the realm, squared a domain ten thousand li on a side, and carved it into ten thousand hundred-li polities—the very epoch the Book of Changes extols when it says, "He who rises first above the throng brings every kingdom to rest."

sentences.zh: 昔在帝堯，協和萬邦，制八家爲鄰，三鄰爲朋，三朋爲里，五里爲邑，十邑爲都，十都爲師，州十有二師焉。

translations.literal: Formerly under Emperor Yao he harmonized the myriad states; he regulated: eight households form a neighborhood, three neighborhoods form a peng, three peng form a li, five li form a yi, ten yi form a du, ten du form a shi, and a province has twelve shi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yao the countries learned concord, and government knit tight: eight families made a street, three streets a cluster, three clusters a ward, five wards a market town, ten such towns a greater burgh, ten burghs a canton, and twelve cantons stitched one province.

sentences.zh: 夏后氏東漸于海，西被于流沙，南浮于江，而朔南暨聲教，窮豎亥所步，莫不率俾，會群臣於塗山，執玉帛者萬國。

translations.literal: The house of Xia eastward reached to the sea, westward extended to the flowing sands, southward floated on the Jiang; north and south likewise were united by culture and teaching, exhausting where Shu Hai had paced; none failed to follow and obey; they assembled the host of lords at Tu Shan; those bearing jade and silk were ten thousand states.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia stretched east until the tide foamed at their feet, west to the shifting sands, south along the great rivers, until their transforming influence ran from pole to pole as far as Shu Hai had ever measured; none refused homage. At Mount Tu they gathered the lords, and ten thousand courts arrived with jade disks and silk.

sentences.zh: 於是九州之內，作爲五服。

translations.literal: Thereupon within the nine provinces they established the five domains (fu).
translations.idiomatic: Within the Nine Provinces they layered five concentric belts of fealty.

sentences.zh: 天子之國，內五百里甸服，百里賦納總，二百里納銍，三百里納秸服，四百里粟，五百里米。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's state: the inner five hundred li is the royal domain; at one hundred li tribute is delivered as bound sheaves in the husk; at two hundred li sickle-cut ears; at three hundred li straw and corvée service; at four hundred li millet; at five hundred li rice.
translations.idiomatic: Around the capital ran five hundred li of royal fields: the inner ring sent whole stalks bundled, the next matured heads, the third straw and labor, the fourth threshed grain, the outermost polished rice for the palace kettle.

sentences.zh: 甸服外五百里侯服，百里采，二百里任，三百里候。

translations.literal: Outside the royal domain, five hundred li of marquis-domain: one hundred li of estates, two hundred li of appointments, three hundred li of garrison/watch.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond that stretched another five hundred li of baronial land: the first hundred fed royal manors, the next two hundred supplied ministers of trust, the outer three hundred patrolled the marches.

sentences.zh: 侯服外五百里綏服，三百里揆文教，二百里奮武衛。

translations.literal: Outside the marquis-domain, five hundred li of pacification-domain: three hundred li for adjusting civil teaching and rites, two hundred li for vigorous martial guard.
translations.idiomatic: Next came five hundred li meant to "soothe": three hundred for schools and rites, two hundred bristling with spears that guarded the cordon.

sentences.zh: 綏服外五百里要服，三百里夷，二百里蔡。

translations.literal: Outside the pacification-domain, five hundred li of binding-domain: three hundred li of outer Yi, two hundred li of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the pacified belt lay five hundred li of "treaty" ground—three hundred li of loosely ruled bordermen, two hundred more under banishment law.

sentences.zh: 要服外五百里荒服，三百里蠻，二百里流。

translations.literal: Outside the binding-domain, five hundred li of wild-domain: three hundred li of Man, two hundred li of exile-flow.
translations.idiomatic: The rim was five hundred li of wilderness—three hundred left to rough hill tribes, two hundred reserved for the river of banishment.

sentences.zh: 訖于四海，弼成五服，五服至于五千里。

translations.literal: Reaching to the four seas, they assisted in completing the five domains; the five domains extend to five thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The pattern ran to the four seas, the five girdles locked in place, a full five thousand li from throne to tide-line.

translations.literal: Midway Xia's virtue withered; it encountered the disorder of Youqiong.
translations.idiomatic: Halfway through their age the Xia lost heart, and the realm reeled beneath Youqiong's revolt.

translations.literal: Shaokang raised a restoration; he did not lose the old inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: Shaokang rallied the line and never surrendered the ancestral cauldrons.

sentences.zh: 自孔甲之後，以至于桀，諸侯相兼，其能存者三千餘國，方於塗山，十損其七矣。

translations.literal: From Kong Jia onward, down to Jie, the feudal lords mutually annexed; those able to survive numbered a bit more than three thousand states; compared to Mount Tu, ten lost seven.
translations.idiomatic: From Kong Jia to tyrant Jie the lords devoured one another until barely three thousand states remained—seven in ten had vanished since the great conference at Mount Tu.

sentences.zh: 成湯敗桀於焦，遷鼎於亳，伊摯、仲虺之徒，大明憲典。

translations.literal: Cheng Tang defeated Jie at Jiao, moved the cauldrons to Bo; men such as Yi Zhi and Zhong Hui greatly clarified statutes and models.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Tang broke Jie at Jiao and carried the tripods to Bo; ministers like Yi Yin and Zhong Hui lit clear lamps of law and precedent.

sentences.zh: 王者之制爵祿，公侯伯子男凡五等。

translations.literal: The king's system of enfeoffing ranks and salaries: duke, marquis, earl, viscount, baron—in all five grades.
translations.idiomatic: Royal custom fixed five noble ranks—from duke down to baron—each with its stipend.

sentences.zh: 天子之田方千里，公侯田方百里，伯七十里，子男五十里。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's field is a square of a thousand li; duke and marquis, a square of a hundred li; earl, seventy li; viscount and baron, fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: The king measured a thousand li square; dukes and marquises a hundred, earls seventy, viscounts and barons a bare fifty on a side.

sentences.zh: 不能五十里者，不達於天子，附於諸侯，曰附庸。

translations.literal: Those unable to reach fifty li do not communicate directly with the Son of Heaven; they attach to feudal lords; they are called dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: Polities shy of fifty li could not seek audience alone; they hung on greater lords as client domains.

sentences.zh: 凡四海之內九州，州方千里。

translations.literal: In all, within the four seas are nine provinces; each province is a square of a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Within the four seas lay nine provinces, each a thousand-li square on the chart.

sentences.zh: 州建百里之國三十，七十里之國六十，五十里之國百有二十，凡二百一十國。

translations.literal: In a province are established thirty states of a hundred li, sixty states of seventy li, one hundred twenty states of fifty li—in all two hundred ten states.
translations.idiomatic: Each province raised thirty great hundred-li realms, sixty middling seventy-li counties, and a hundred twenty small fifty-li cells—two hundred ten banners in all.

sentences.zh: 名山大澤不以封，其餘以爲附庸間田。

translations.literal: Famous mountains and great marshes are not used for enfeoffment; the remainder becomes dependencies and interstitial fields.
translations.idiomatic: Crown peaks and imperial bogs never left the king's ledger; leftover patches became vassal pockets and buffer strips.

translations.literal: Eight provinces—each province two hundred ten states.
translations.idiomatic: Eight of the nine provinces repeated that pattern—two hundred ten states apiece.

sentences.zh: 天子之縣內，百里之國九，七十里之國二十有一，五十里之國六十有三，凡九十三國。

translations.literal: Within the Son of Heaven's direct counties: nine states of a hundred li, twenty-one states of seventy li, sixty-three states of fifty li—in all ninety-three states.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the royal demesne itself stood nine hundred-li seats, twenty-one seventy-li manors, and sixty-three fifty-li plots—ninety-three realms devoted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 名山大澤不以班，其餘以祿士，以爲間田。

translations.literal: Famous mountains and great marshes are not parceled out in enfeoffment; the remainder is used to salary officers and becomes interstitial fields.
translations.idiomatic: Sacred heights and royal marshes were never fiefed away; the scraps paid stipendiary officials and plugged holes between grants.

sentences.zh: 凡九州，千七百七十三國。

translations.literal: In all the nine provinces: one thousand seven hundred seventy-three states.
translations.idiomatic: Across the Nine Provinces the tallies listed one thousand seven hundred seventy-three states.

sentences.zh: 天子之元士，諸侯之附庸，不與。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's chief knights and the feudal lords' dependencies are not included.
translations.idiomatic: The count omits the king's senior householders and the petty clients of great barons.

sentences.zh: 天子百里之內以供官，千里之內以爲御，千里之外設方伯。

translations.literal: Within the Son of Heaven's hundred li, for supplying officials; within a thousand li, for court provision; beyond a thousand li, regional hegemons are appointed.
translations.idiomatic: The inner hundred li fed the bureaucracy, the thousand li stocked palace service, and beyond that the king set regional elders to rule in his stead.

translations.literal: Five states form a dependency-group; a dependency-group has a chief.
translations.idiomatic: Five states formed a dependency cluster led by a chief.

translations.literal: Ten states form a chain; a chain has a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Ten states formed a league placed under a captain.

translations.literal: Thirty states form a corps; a corps has a director.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty states formed a corps overseen by a senior marshal.

sentences.zh: 二百一十國以爲州，州有伯。

translations.literal: Two hundred ten states form a province; a province has a bo.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred ten states formed a province ruled by a regional elder.

sentences.zh: 八州，八伯，五十六正，百六十八帥，三百三十六長。

translations.literal: Eight provinces: eight bo, fifty-six directors, one hundred sixty-eight commanders, three hundred thirty-six chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Eight provinces meant eight great lords, fifty-six marshals, one hundred sixty-eight captains, and three hundred thirty-six village heads.

sentences.zh: 八伯各以其屬屬於天子之老二人，分天下爲左右，曰二伯。

translations.literal: Each of the eight bo with his dependents attaches to two elders of the Son of Heaven; they divide the realm into left and right, called the two bo.
translations.idiomatic: Each provincial lord knelt to one of the king's two senior regents, splitting the world into eastern and western halves—the Two Chiefs of high Zhou.

sentences.zh: 千里之內曰甸，千里之外曰采，曰流。

translations.literal: Within a thousand li is called dian; beyond a thousand li is called cai and liu.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the thousand-li cordon lay the royal hearths; outside stretched ministerial estates and the flowing lands of exile.

sentences.zh: 天子使其大夫爲三監，監於方伯之國，國三人。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven causes his great officers to be triple overseers; they oversee in the regional hegemons' states; three men per state.
translations.idiomatic: The king posted three-man inspectorates in every regional capital to eye the barons for him.

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's counties: inwardly, they are stipendiary fiefs for feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Domains hugging the throne were stipendiary grants to great lords.

translations.literal: Outwardly, they are inheriting lineages of feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Those farther out settled into noble lines handed down through inheritance.

sentences.zh: 武王歸豐，監於二代，設爵惟五，分土惟三。

translations.literal: King Wu returned to Feng, examined the two dynasties, established ranks only five, divided land only three grades.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu withdrew to Feng, studied Xia and Shang, fixed five noble rows, and sorted fief size into three steps.

sentences.zh: 封同姓五十餘國，周公、康叔建於魯衛，各數百里。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed kinsmen fifty-odd states; the Duke of Zhou and Kang Shu were established at Lu and Wei, each several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: He planted more than fifty Zhou princes across the map—the Duke of Zhou at Lu, Kang Shu at Wei—each commanding several hundred li.

sentences.zh: 太公封於齊，表東海者也。

translations.literal: Grand Duke Tai was enfeoffed at Qi—he who screens the eastern sea.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Gong took Qi as his shield against the eastern tide.

sentences.zh: 凡一千八百國，布列於五千里內。

translations.literal: In all one thousand eight hundred states, arrayed within five thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen hundred realms checkered the five-thousand-li heartland.

sentences.zh: 而太昊、黃帝之後，唐虞侯伯猶存。

translations.literal: Moreover descendants of Taihao and the Yellow Emperor—Tang-Yao era marquises and earls—still survived.
translations.idiomatic: Lines sprung from Taihao and the Yellow Emperor, marquises who remembered Yao and Shun, still clung to titles in that new Zhou dawn.

sentences.zh: 大司徒以諸公之地封疆方五百里，其食者半；

translations.literal: The grand steward: the lands of the dukes have boundaries a square of five hundred li; of it half provides revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education carved dukes five hundred li square but let them tax only half the soil;

sentences.zh: 諸侯之地方四百里，其食者參之一；

translations.literal: The lands of marquises are four hundred li square; of them one third provides revenue.
translations.idiomatic: marquises held four hundred li yet drew a third to their kitchens;

sentences.zh: 諸伯之地方三百里，其食者參之一；

translations.literal: The lands of earls are three hundred li square; of them one third provides revenue.
translations.idiomatic: earls kept three hundred li with the same third rule;

sentences.zh: 諸子之地方二百里，其食者四之一；

translations.literal: The lands of viscounts are two hundred li square; of them one quarter provides revenue.
translations.idiomatic: viscounts two hundred li but spent only a quarter;

sentences.zh: 諸男之地方百里，其食者四之一。

translations.literal: The lands of barons are a hundred li square; of them one quarter provides revenue.
translations.idiomatic: barons a bare hundred li yet owned a quarter of the yield.

sentences.zh: 不易之地家百畝，一易之地家二百畝，再易之地家三百畝。

translations.literal: On land that does not rotate, a household receives a hundred mu; on land rotated once, two hundred mu; on land rotated twice, three hundred mu.
translations.idiomatic: Permanent fields granted a household a hundred mu, once-fallow soil two hundred, and thrice-tired ground three hundred so the tax base stayed even.

translations.literal: Five households form a bi; they are caused mutually to guarantee.
translations.idiomatic: Five families swore mutual bail;

translations.literal: Five bi form a lü; they are caused mutually to shelter.
translations.idiomatic: five such rings a lane that housed the homeless;

translations.literal: Four lü form a zu; they are caused mutually to bury.
translations.idiomatic: four lanes a clan burying its dead together;

translations.literal: Five zu form a dang; they are caused mutually to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: five clans a company that rushed to fires and raids;

translations.literal: Five dang form a zhou; they are caused mutually to relieve.
translations.idiomatic: five companies a canton pooling famine grain;

translations.literal: Five zhou form a xiang; they are caused mutually to observe guest ritual.
translations.idiomatic: five cantons a countryside whose elders still bowed in guest-rite.

sentences.zh: 小司徒以五人爲伍，五伍爲兩，四兩爲卒，五卒爲旅，五旅爲師，五師爲軍。

translations.literal: The lesser steward: by five men a squad, five squads a pair, four pairs a company, five companies a battalion, five battalions a division, five divisions an army.
translations.idiomatic: The junior steward stacked squads: five men a file, five files a pair, four pairs a company, five companies a battalion, five battalions a host, five hosts the full army.

sentences.zh: 以起軍旅，以作田役，以比追胥，以令貢賦。

translations.literal: By this raise armies, perform field labor and corvée, compare pursuit and night patrol, order tribute and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Those ladders raised campaigns, drafted ditch gangs, mustered night watchmen, and split the grain and corvée rolls.

sentences.zh: 乃經土地而井牧其田野，九夫爲井，四井爲邑，四邑爲丘，四丘爲甸，四甸爲縣，四縣爲都。

translations.literal: Then they surveyed land and well-and-pastured the fields and wilds: nine husbands a well, four wells a settlement, four settlements a mound, four mounds a dian, four dian a county, four counties a metropolis.
translations.idiomatic: Surveyors laid the well-net: nine farmers to a well, four wells a hamlet, four hamlets a hill-girdle, four hill-girdles a parcel, four parcels a county, four counties a great city.

sentences.zh: 遺人則十里有廬，廬有飲食。

translations.literal: The supply officer: then every ten li has a hut; the hut has drink and food.
translations.idiomatic: Wayfarers found a lodge every ten li with water and a warm bowl.

sentences.zh: 三十里有宿，宿有路室，路室有委。

translations.literal: Every thirty li has a lodging; the lodging has roadside chambers; the roadside chambers have stored provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Every thirty li brought a full station, roadside cells, and stacked grain.

sentences.zh: 五十里有市，市有候，候有館，館有積。

translations.literal: Every fifty li has a market; the market has a post; the post has a lodge; the lodge has accumulations.
translations.idiomatic: Every fifty li markets bustled with guard posts, guest halls, and piled stores.

sentences.zh: 遂人則五家爲鄰，五鄰爲里，四里爲酇，五酇爲鄙，五鄙爲縣，五縣爲遂。

translations.literal: The field officer: five households form lin, five lin a li, four li a zan, five zan a bi, five bi a county, five counties a sui.
translations.idiomatic: Rural marshals wove five homes into a lane, five lanes a hamlet, four hamlets a township, five townships a patch, five patches a county, five counties a sui belt.

sentences.zh: 大司馬以九畿之籍，施邦國之政。

translations.literal: The grand marshal, by the registers of the nine ji, applies governance to the states.
translations.idiomatic: The war minister read the nine belts girding Wangcheng and from them spun every lord's marching orders.

sentences.zh: 方千里曰國畿，其外方五百里曰侯畿，又其外方五百里曰甸畿，又其外方五百里曰男畿，又其外方五百里曰采畿，又其外方五百里曰衛畿，又其外方五百里曰蠻畿，又其外方五百里曰夷畿，又其外方五百里曰鎮畿，又其外方五百里曰藩畿。

translations.literal: A square of a thousand li is called the royal ji; its outer square of five hundred li is the marquis ji; again outside five hundred li is the dian ji; again outside five hundred li is the male-rank ji; again outside five hundred li is the stipend ji; again outside five hundred li is the guard ji; again outside five hundred li is the man ji; again outside five hundred li is the yi ji; again outside five hundred li is the garrison ji; again outside five hundred li is the vassal-screen ji.
translations.idiomatic: The capital sat in a thousand-li square; then nine half-thousand-li rings unrolled—baronial fields, royal estates, male fiefs, salary lands, guard strips, southern wilds, eastern wilds, garrison marches, and a final curtain of outer vassals.

translations.literal: 〈Ji means the field limit.
translations.idiomatic: The marginal note explains that ji denotes the border of taxable fields.

sentences.zh: 自王城以外，面五千里爲界，有分限者九也。〉

translations.literal: From outside the royal city, on each face five thousand li is the boundary; there are nine division-limits.〉
translations.idiomatic: It adds that from the royal walls each quarter runs five thousand li, ringed by nine stepped partitions.

sentences.zh: 于時治致太平，政稱刑措，民口千三百七十一萬四千九百三十三，蓋周之盛者也。

translations.literal: At that time rule attained the Great Peace, government was called punishments set aside, the people's mouths numbered thirteen million seven hundred fourteen thousand nine hundred thirty-three—this was the height of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: That age ripened into the Great Peace, the racks stood empty, and the census inked 13,714,933 names—a Zhou summer at flood tide.

sentences.zh: 其衰也，則禮樂征伐出自諸侯，強吞弱而眾暴寡。

translations.literal: In its decline, then rites, music, expeditions, and punitive attacks issued from the feudal lords; the strong swallowed the weak and the many tyrannized the few.
translations.idiomatic: When it rotted, drums and odes marched under barons' banners, strong states swallowed weak neighbors, and packs harried the lone.

sentences.zh: 春秋之初，尚有千二百國，迄獲麟之末，二百四十二年，弒君三十六，亡國五十二，諸侯奔走不得保其社稷者不可勝數，而見於春秋經傳者百有七十國焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Spring and Autumn there were still one thousand two hundred states; down to the end of capturing the unicorn, two hundred forty-two years, regicide of lords thirty-six, perished states fifty-two, feudal lords fleeing unable to preserve their altars—uncountable; yet those appearing in the Spring and Autumn classic and commentaries numbered one hundred seventy states.
translations.idiomatic: Early Spring and Autumn still counted twelve hundred flags; by the day Confucius penned the unicorn's close—two hundred forty-two bloodied years—thirty-six kings had been knifed, fifty-two realms snuffed, and numberless lords fled ruined shrines, though the classic and its gloss remember only one hundred seventy names.

translations.literal: One hundred thirty-nine know where they dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred thirty-nine of them still have identifiable capitals on the map.

sentences.zh: 〈魯、邾、鄭、宋、紀、衛、西虢、莒、齊、陳、杞、蔡、邢、郕、晉、薛、許、鄧、秦、曹、楚、隨、黃、梁、虞、鄖、小邾、徐、燕、鄀、麋、舒、庸、郯、萊、吳、越、有窮、三苗、瓜州、有虞、東虢、共、宿、申、夷、向、南燕、滕、凡、戴、息、郜、芮、魏、淳于、穀、巴、州、蓼、羅、賴、牟、葛、譚、蕭、遂、滑、權、鄣、霍、耿、江、冀、弦、道、柏、微、鄫、厲、項、密、任、須句、顓臾、頓、管、雍、畢、豐、邘、應、蔣、茅、胙、夔、介、焦、沈、六、巢、根牟、唐、黎、郇瑕、寒、有鬲、斟灌、斟尋、過、有過、戈、偪陽、邿、鑄、豕韋、唐杜、楊、豳、鄶、觀、扈、邳、胡、黎、大庭、駘、岐、邶、鍾吾、蒲姑、昆吾、房、密須、甲父、鄅、桐、亳、韓、趙。〉

translations.literal: 〈Lu, Zhu, Zheng, Song, Ji, Wei, Western Guo, Ju, Qi, Chen, Qi, Cai, Xing, Cheng, Jin, Xue, Xu, Deng, Qin, Cao, Chu, Sui, Huang, Liang, Yu, Yun, Lesser Zhu, Xu, Yan, Ruo, Mi, Shu, Yong, Tan, Lai, Wu, Yue, Youqiong, Sanmiao, Guazhou, You Yu, Eastern Guo, Gong, Su, Shen, Yi, Xiang, Southern Yan, Teng, Fan, Dai, Xi, Gao, Rui, Wei, Chunyu, Gu, Ba, Zhou, Liao, Luo, Lai, Mou, Ge, Tan, Xiao, Sui, Hua, Quan, Zhang, Huo, Geng, Jiang, Ji, Xian, Dao, Bo, Wei, Zeng, Li, Xiang, Mi, Ren, Xuqu, Zhuanyu, Dun, Guan, Yong, Bi, Feng, Yu, Ying, Jiang, Mao, Zuo, Kui, Jie, Jiao, Shen, Liu, Chao, Genmou, Tang, Li, Xunxia, Han, Youge, Zhuguan, Zhunxun, Guo, Youguo, Ge, Biyang, Shi, Zhu, Shangwei, Tang Du, Yang, Bin, Kuai, Guan, Hu, Li, Danting, Tai, Qi, Bei, Zhongwu, Pugu, Kunwu, Fang, Mixu, Jiafu, Yu, Tong, Bo, Han, Zhao.〉
translations.idiomatic: The commentary enumerates every one of the one hundred thirty-nine states whose capitals can still be placed—from Lu, Zhu, Zheng, and Song through Wu, Yue, Qin, Chu, Jin, Qi, Yan, and Zhao, down to tiny polities such as Ge, Biyang, and Kunwu—so that later readers can still plot the Spring and Autumn chessboard.

translations.literal: Thirty-one states utterly lost their locations.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-one others vanished so completely that their very sites are forgotten.

sentences.zh: 〈祭、極、荀、賈、貳、軫、絞、於餘丘、陽、箕、英氏、毛、聃、莘、偪、封父、仍、有仍、崇、鄟、庸、姺、奄、商奄、褒姒、蓐、有緡、闕鞏、飂、鬷、窮桑。〉

translations.literal: 〈Zhai, Ji, Xun, Jia, Er, Zhen, Jiao, Yuyuqiu, Yang, Ji, Ying, Mao, Dan, Shen, Bi, Fengfu, Reng, Youreng, Chong, Tuan, Yong, Shen, Yan, Shangyan, Baosi, Ru, Youmin, Quegong, Liu, Zong, Qiongsang.〉
translations.idiomatic: The thirty-one states whose very sites are lost are named here as well—Zhai, Ji, Xun, Jia, Er, Zhen, Jiao, Yuyuqiu, Yang, Ji, Ying, Mao, Dan, Shen, Bi, Fengfu, Reng, Youreng, Chong, Tuan, Yong, Shen, Yan, Shangyan, Baosi, Ru, Youmin, Quegong, Liu, Zong, and Qiongsang—so that not even a ghost capital slips from the record.

translations.literal: The Man, Yi, Rong, and Di are not among these.
translations.idiomatic: Southern, eastern, western, and northern tribes were never part of that roll.

translations.literal: The Five Hegemons rose in succession; they oversaw their covenants and assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: Five overlords rose in turn to chair the league altars and stamp clan oaths.

sentences.zh: 陵夷至于戰國，遂有七王，

translations.literal: Declining further, it reached the Warring States; thereupon there were seven kings,
translations.idiomatic: The slide ran on into the Warring States, and seven crowned powers shouldered the world—

translations.literal: (Han, Wei, Zhao, Yan, Qi, Qin, Chu.)
translations.idiomatic: Han, Wei, Zhao, Yan, Qi, Qin, and Chu.

sentences.zh: 又有宋、衛、中山，不斷如綫，如三晉篡奪，亦稱孤也。

translations.literal: Moreover there were Song, Wei, and Zhongshan, unbroken like a thread; as for the usurpations of the three Jin, they also called themselves orphaned rulers.
translations.idiomatic: Song, Wei, and Zhongshan still hung by a thread, while the breakaway triplets of Jin stole the mandate yet whimpered that they ruled as orphaned heirs.

sentences.zh: 《司馬法》廣陳三代，曰：古者六尺爲步，步百爲畝，畝百爲夫，夫三爲屋，屋三爲井。

translations.literal: The "Sima Fa" broadly expounds the Three Dynasties, saying: In antiquity six chi made a pace, a hundred paces made a mu, a hundred mu made a husband-unit, three husband-units made a roof-cluster, three roof-clusters made a well-field.
translations.idiomatic: The Military Canons of Sima recount the Three Ages: six feet to the pace, a hundred paces to the survey mu, a hundred mu to a husband's share, three husbands to a cluster, three clusters to the sacred well of nine farms.

sentences.zh: 井方一里，是爲九夫，八家共之。

translations.literal: A well is a square of one li; this constitutes nine husband-slots; eight households share it.
translations.idiomatic: Each well squared a li, carved nine strips, and yoked eight families to its central lord's strip.

sentences.zh: 一夫一婦受私田百畝，公田十畝，是爲八百八十畝，餘二十畝爲廬舍，出入相友，守望相助，疾病相救。

translations.literal: One husband one wife receive private fields a hundred mu, public field ten mu—this makes eight hundred eighty mu; the remaining twenty mu are hut-sites; going out and entering they befriend; watching and guarding they assist; in sickness they rescue one another.
translations.idiomatic: Each couple drew a hundred private mu and ten for the common furrow—880 mu under tillage and twenty for roofs; neighbors pledged friendship at every gate, stood night watch together, and nursed fevers shoulder to shoulder.

sentences.zh: 民受田，上田夫百畝，中田夫二百畝，下田夫三百畝，歲受耕之，爰自其處。

translations.literal: The people receive fields: on upper fields a husband has a hundred mu; on middle fields two hundred mu; on lower fields three hundred mu; yearly they receive and till them, shifting accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers drew graded plots—one hundred mu on rich soil, two hundred on middling, three hundred on lean—rotating with the seasons as the law nudged them along.

sentences.zh: 其家眾男爲餘夫，亦以口受田如此。

translations.literal: The family's multitude of males as surplus husbands likewise by mouth receive fields in this manner.
translations.idiomatic: Extra grown sons counted as surplus tillers and earned more acreage by the same mouth tally.

sentences.zh: 士工商家受田，五口乃當農夫一口。

translations.literal: Scholar, artisan, and merchant households receive fields; five mouths equal one peasant mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry, craftsmen, and merchants held land too, yet five of their mouths paid as one plowman's share.

sentences.zh: 有賦有稅，稅謂公田什一及工商衡虞之入也，賦供車馬甲兵士從之役。

translations.literal: There are fu and shui; shui means the public-field one-tenth and the income of artisans, merchants, weighers, and marsh-keepers; fu supplies chariots, horses, armor, weapons, accompanyers, and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Two ledgers ran: "tax" skimmed the lord's tenth and the townsmen who trafficked scales and marshes; "levy" horseshoed chariots, buckled armor, and dragooned footmen.

sentences.zh: 民年二十受田，六十歸田。

translations.literal: The people at age twenty receive fields; at sixty they return fields.
translations.idiomatic: A man took land at twenty and surrendered it at sixty.

sentences.zh: 種穀必雜五種，以備災旱。

translations.literal: Planting grain must mix five kinds, to prepare for disaster and drought.
translations.idiomatic: Every field blended five grains so famine could not kill the harvest whole.

sentences.zh: 田中不得有樹，以妨五穀。

translations.literal: In fields there must not be trees, lest they obstruct the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: Grain land stayed shadeless—no orchard stealing sunlight from the staples.

sentences.zh: 環廬種桑柘，菜茹有畦，瓜瓠果蓏植於疆埸，雞㹠狗豕無失其時。

translations.literal: Around huts plant mulberry and zhe; vegetables have beds; melons, gourds, fruits, and berries plant on boundaries; chickens, pigs, dogs, and swine—do not miss their seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Mulberries hugged each roof, kitchen gardens squared their rows, melons straggled along the headlands, and every yard timed its fowl and hogs to the turning moons.

sentences.zh: 閭有序，鄉有庠，序以明教，庠以行禮。

translations.literal: A lü has a village school; a xiang has a hall; the village school clarifies teaching; the hall conducts rites.
translations.idiomatic: Each lane kept a school where royal lessons shone, each district a hall where elders rehearsed ceremony.

sentences.zh: 司馬之法，官設六軍之眾，因井田而制軍。

translations.literal: The Sima method: officials establish the mass of six armies; according to well-fields they regulate armies.
translations.idiomatic: The war statutes called up six hosts, threading regiment on regiment straight from the well-field grid.

sentences.zh: 令地方一里爲井，井十爲通，通十爲成，成方十里。

translations.literal: They ordered the land: a square of one li makes a well-field; ten wells make a tong; ten tong make a cheng; a cheng is a square of ten li.
translations.idiomatic: The statute squared the soil into one-li well-fields, stacked ten wells into a tong, ten tong into a cheng block ten li on a side.

sentences.zh: 成十爲終，終十爲同，同方百里。

translations.literal: Ten cheng make a zhong; ten zhong make a tong; a tong is a square of a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Ten cheng units formed a zhong, ten zhong a tong, and each tong measured a hundred li square.

sentences.zh: 同十爲封，封十爲畿，畿方千里。

translations.literal: Ten tong make a feng; ten feng make ji; ji is a square of a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Ten tong made a feng barony, ten feng made the royal ji belt, and the ji itself stretched a thousand li on a side.

sentences.zh: 故井四爲邑，邑四爲丘，丘十六井，有戎馬一匹，牛三頭。

translations.literal: Therefore four wells make a yi; four yi make a qiu; a qiu sixteen wells—has one war horse, three ox heads.
translations.idiomatic: Four wells formed a hamlet, four hamlets a mound-unit of sixteen wells, stocked with one cavalry mount and three oxen.

sentences.zh: 四丘爲甸，甸六十四井也，有戎馬四匹，兵車一乘，牛十二頭，甲士三人，卒七十二人。

translations.literal: Four qiu make a dian; a dian sixty-four wells—has four war horses, one chariot team, twelve ox heads, three armored warriors, seventy-two foot soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Four mound-units made a dian of sixty-four wells, enough for four mounts, one war chariot, twelve oxen, three armored guards, and seventy-two footmen.

translations.literal: This is called the chariot-team regulation.
translations.idiomatic: That was the reckoning behind each chariot levy.

sentences.zh: 一同百里，提封萬井，除山川、坑岸、城池、邑居、園囿、街路三千六百井，定出賦六千四百井，戎馬四百匹，兵車百乘，此卿大夫菜地之大者也，是謂百乘之家。

translations.literal: One tong a hundred li—enveloping ten thousand wells; excluding mountains, rivers, pits, banks, city walls, towns, orchards, parks, streets, roads—three thousand six hundred wells; fixed outgoing tax six thousand four hundred wells; four hundred war horses; one hundred chariot teams—this is the great of minister and great officer vegetable-lands; it is called a hundred-chariot household.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred-li tong claimed ten thousand nominal wells; after carving out hills, rivers, towns, and roads, six thousand four hundred wells paid the corvée, yielding four hundred horses and a hundred chariots—the great ministerial estate called a "hundred-chariot" house.

sentences.zh: 一封三百六十六里，提封十萬井，定出賦六萬四千井，戎馬四千匹，兵車千乘，此謂諸侯之大者也，謂之千乘之國。

translations.literal: One feng three hundred sixty-six li—enveloping one hundred thousand wells; fixed outgoing tax sixty-four thousand wells; four thousand war horses; one thousand chariot teams—this is called the great of feudal lords; it is called a thousand-chariot state.
translations.idiomatic: A feng of 366 li wrapped a hundred thousand wells on paper, sixty-four thousand of them taxable, supporting four thousand horses and a thousand chariots—the scale of a great feudal lord, a true "thousand-chariot" kingdom.

sentences.zh: 天子畿內方千里，提封百萬井，定出賦六十四萬井，戎馬四萬匹，兵車萬乘，戎卒七十二萬人，故天子稱萬乘之主焉。

translations.literal: Within the Son of Heaven's ji a square of a thousand li—enveloping a million wells; fixed outgoing tax six hundred forty thousand wells; forty thousand war horses; ten thousand chariot teams; seven hundred twenty thousand martial soldiers—therefore the Son of Heaven is called lord of ten thousand chariots.
translations.idiomatic: The royal thousand-li core listed a million wells, taxed six hundred forty thousand of them, and could field forty thousand horses, ten thousand chariot teams, and seven hundred twenty thousand troops—why the king is styled lord of "ten thousand chariots."

sentences.zh: 秦始皇既得志於天下，訪周之敗，以爲處士橫議，諸侯尋戈，四夷交侵，以弱見奪，於是削去五等焉。

translations.literal: Qin Shihuang, having obtained his aim under heaven, investigated Zhou's defeat; he thought wandering scholars debated recklessly, feudal lords soon took up spears, the four Yi mutually invaded, and by weakness was seized—thereupon cut away the five ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Once the First Emperor owned the realm he studied why Zhou fell: wandering scholars had stirred debate, barons had raised arms, border peoples had pressed in, and weakness invited seizure—so he abolished the five noble grades altogether.

sentences.zh: 漢興，創艾亡秦孤立而敗，於是割裂封疆，立爵二等，功臣侯者百有餘邑。

translations.literal: Han rose, chastened by perished Qin's isolation and defeat; thereupon carved and split enfeoffed boundaries, established two grades of rank; meritorious subjects enfeoffed as marquises were a bit more than a hundred towns.
translations.idiomatic: The Han founders, smarting from Qin's lonely collapse, sliced the map anew, kept only two noble ranks, and enfeoffed a hundred-odd marquisates for their generals and ministers.

sentences.zh: 于時民罹秦項，戶口彫弊，大侯不過萬家，小者五六百戶，而尊王子弟，大啟九國。

translations.literal: At that time the people suffered Qin and Xiang; households and mouths were withered and exhausted; great marquises did not exceed ten thousand families, small ones five or six hundred households—yet they honored royal sons and younger brothers, greatly opening nine states.
translations.idiomatic: The people were still scarred by Qin and Xiang Yu, so even great marquises counted fewer than ten thousand families and small ones only five or six hundred—yet the throne showered honors on imperial kinsmen and flung open nine huge kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 古者有分土而無分民，若乃大者跨州連郡，小則十有餘城，以戶口爲差降，略封疆之遠近，所謂分民自漢始也。

translations.literal: In antiquity there was dividing soil but not dividing people; as for then, large ones spanned provinces linking commanderies, small ones still had more than ten cities; by households and mouths as gradations, roughly ignoring enfeoffed boundaries' distance or nearness—what is called dividing the people began from Han.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity parceled land, not subjects; now great fiefs swallowed whole provinces while small ones still held ten walled towns, ranked by headcount instead of true distance—"sharing out the people" really began under Han.

sentences.zh: 起雁門以東，盡遼陽，爲燕代。

translations.literal: From Yanmen eastward, exhaustively to Liaoyang, was Yan-Dai.
translations.idiomatic: From Yanmen east to the Liaoyang coast became the Yan and Dai bloc.

sentences.zh: 常山以南，太行左轉，渡河濟，漸于海，爲齊趙。

translations.literal: South of Changshan, Taihang turning left, crossing the Yellow River and the Ji, reaching to the sea, was Qi-Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: South of Changshan the Taihang swung east, the realm crossed the Yellow River and the Ji River, and the land ran down to the sea as Qi and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 穀泗以注，奄有龜蒙，爲梁楚。

translations.literal: Gu and Si pour in; broadly possessing Gui and Meng—was Liang-Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Where the Gu and Si rivers drain, taking in Mount Gui and Mount Meng, lay Liang and Chu.

sentences.zh: 東帶江湖，薄會稽，爲荊吳。

translations.literal: East belted by the Jiang and lakes, pressing on Kuaiji—was Jing-Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The belt of great rivers and lakes eastward to Kuaiji formed Jing and Wu.

sentences.zh: 北界淮瀕，略廬衡，爲淮南。

translations.literal: North bounded by the Huai's brink, taking Lu and Heng—was Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: North along the Huai, sweeping Mount Lu and Mount Heng, sat Huainan.

sentences.zh: 波漢之陽，亙九疑，爲長沙。

translations.literal: Rippling the Han's south, spanning the Nine Doubts—was Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Han, strung along the Nine Doubts peaks, was Changsha.

sentences.zh: 諸侯比境，周匝三垂，外接胡越。

translations.literal: The feudal lords' borders adjoined; they circled the three margins; outwardly they connected Hu and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdoms shared borders, wrapped the inner realm on three sides, and pressed outward against the Hu and Yue frontiers.

sentences.zh: 天子自有三河、東郡、潁川、南陽，自江陵以西至巴蜀，北至雲中，西至隴西，與京師內史，凡十五郡。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven himself possessed the Three Rivers, Dong commandery, Yingchuan, Nanyang; from Jiangling westward to Ba-Shu, north to Yunzhong, west to Longxi, together with the capital metropolitan intendant—in all fifteen commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The throne kept the Three Rivers belt, Dong, Yingchuan, and Nanyang, the arc from Jiangling west into Ba and Shu, the northern rim to Yunzhong, the western rim to Longxi, plus the inner capital districts—fifteen commanderies in all.

sentences.zh: 文帝采賈生之議分齊趙，景帝用朝錯之計削吳楚。

translations.literal: Wendi adopted Jia Sheng's proposal to divide Qi and Zhao; Jingdi employed Chao Cuo's plan to pare Wu and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen followed Jia Yi's advice to split Qi and Zhao; Emperor Jing used Chao Cuo's scheme to shave away Wu and Chu.

sentences.zh: 武帝施主父之冊，下推恩之令，使諸侯王得分戶邑以封子弟，不行黜陟，而藩國自析。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu applied Zhufu's tablets, issued the push-grace edict, causing kings of feudal states to be able to divide household towns to enfeoff sons and younger brothers; without carrying out demotions and promotions, the screen states split themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu adopted Zhufu's memorial and promulgated the "extending grace" edict so kings could parcel towns among sons—no overt demotions were needed, yet every great kingdom quietly fell apart.

sentences.zh: 自此以來，齊分爲七，趙分爲六，梁分爲五，淮南分爲三。

translations.literal: From this time onward, Qi split into seven, Zhao into six, Liang into five, Huainan into three.
translations.idiomatic: After that Qi shattered into seven fragments, Zhao into six, Liang into five, and Huainan into three.

sentences.zh: 皇子始立者大國不過十餘城，長沙、燕、代雖有舊名，皆亡南北邊矣。

translations.literal: Imperial sons first established: great states did not exceed ten-odd cities; Changsha, Yan, and Dai, although having old names, all lost south and north borders.
translations.idiomatic: Newly enfeoffed princes held at best a dozen towns, and storied names like Changsha, Yan, and Dai no longer guarded the old northern and southern marches.

sentences.zh: 自文景與民休息，至平帝元始二年，民戶千二百二十三萬三千六十二，口五千九百五十九萬四千九百七十八，其地東西九千三百二里，南北萬三千三百六十八里。

translations.literal: From Wen and Jing giving the people rest, down to Emperor Ping's Yuanshi second year, the people's households were twelve million two hundred thirty-three thousand sixty-two, mouths fifty-nine million five hundred ninety-four thousand nine hundred seventy-eight; the territory east-west nine thousand three hundred two li, north-south thirteen thousand three hundred sixty-eight li.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wen-Jing recovery to the second year of Yuansheng under Emperor Ping, the census recorded 12,233,062 households and 59,594,978 persons on a domain stretching 9,302 li east-west and 13,368 li north-south.

translations.literal: In general every ten li one ting; a ting has a chief.
translations.idiomatic: Roughly every ten li stood a waystation with its headman.

sentences.zh: 十亭一鄉，鄉有三老，有秩嗇夫、游徼各一人。

translations.literal: Ten ting one xiang; a xiang has three elders, one ranked overseer, one patrol scout each.
translations.idiomatic: Ten stations made a township with three elders, a salaried overseer, and a roving constable.

sentences.zh: 縣大率方百里，民稠則減，稀則曠，鄉亭亦如之。

translations.literal: A county in general is a square of a hundred li; if people dense then reduce, if sparse then enlarge; xiang and ting likewise so.
translations.idiomatic: A county normally squared a hundred li, shrinking where crowded and swelling where empty, with townships and stations adjusted the same way.

translations.literal: All are Qin institutions.
translations.idiomatic: All of this followed Qin blueprints.

sentences.zh: 光武中興，不踰前制，東海王彊以去就有禮，故優以大封，兼食魯郡二十九縣，其餘稱爲寵錫者，兼一郡而已。

translations.literal: Guangwu's restoration did not exceed the former system; the Prince of the Eastern Sea, Qiang, because of going and staying with propriety, therefore was favored with a great enfeoffment, concurrently eating twenty-nine counties of Lu commandery; the rest called favored grants were at most one commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu's revival kept Han's old ceilings; only Prince Qiang of Donghai, for yielding his claim with grace, won a super-fief that swallowed twenty-nine Lu counties, while other royal favors rarely exceeded a single commandery.

sentences.zh: 至桓帝永壽三年，戶千六十七萬七千九百六十，口五千六百四十八萬六千八百五十六，[3]斯亦戶口之滋殖者也。

translations.literal: Down to Emperor Huan's Yongshou third year, households ten million six hundred seventy-seven thousand nine hundred sixty, mouths fifty-six million four hundred eighty-six thousand eight hundred fifty-six, [3] this too is the increase and multiplication of households and mouths.
translations.idiomatic: By Yongshou 3 under Emperor Huan the registers showed 10,677,960 households and 56,486,856 people[3]—another surge in the population rolls.

sentences.zh: 獻帝建安元年拜曹操爲鎮東將軍，封費亭侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Xian Jian'an first year enfeoffed Cao Cao as General Who Stabilizes the East, enfeoffed Feiting precinct marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jian'an Emperor Xian named Cao Cao General Who Pacifies the East and made him Marquis of Feiting Precinct.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初三年，初制封王之庶子爲鄉公，嗣王之庶子爲亭侯，[4]公侯之庶子爲亭伯。

translations.literal: Wei Wendi Huangchu third year, first regulated enfeoffing kings' bastard sons as township dukes, inheriting kings' bastard sons as precinct marquises, [4] dukes' and marquises' bastard sons as precinct earls.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 3 Cao Pi decreed that a king's younger sons became township dukes, an heir-apparent king's younger sons precinct marquises,[4] and younger sons of dukes and marquises precinct earls.

sentences.zh: 劉備章武元年，亦以郡國封建諸王，或遙採嘉名，不由檢土地所出。

translations.literal: Liu Bei Zhangwu first year, likewise by commanderies and kingdoms enfeoffed the various kings; sometimes distantly adopting fine names, not following inspection of what the land produced.
translations.idiomatic: In his first Zhangwu year Liu Bei also enfeoffed princes across commanderies, sometimes borrowing glamorous old names without regard to what the soil actually yielded.

sentences.zh: 其戶二十萬，男女口九十萬。

translations.literal: Its households two hundred thousand, male and female mouths nine hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shu at that count held two hundred thousand households and nine hundred thousand souls.

sentences.zh: 孫權赤烏五年，亦取中州嘉號封建諸王。

translations.literal: Sun Quan Chiwu fifth year, likewise took central-plain fine titles to enfeoff the various kings.
translations.idiomatic: In Chiwu 5 Sun Quan likewise raided the old Central Plain style of noble titles for his princes.

sentences.zh: 其戶五十二萬三千，男女口二百四十萬。

translations.literal: Its households five hundred twenty-three thousand, male and female mouths two million four hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wu then counted 523,000 households and 2,400,000 people.

sentences.zh: 晉文帝爲晉王，命裴秀等建立五等之制，惟安平郡公孚邑萬戶，制度如魏諸王。
