translations.literal: Jin Wendi as Prince of Jin ordered Pei Xiu and others to establish the five-rank system; only the Commandery Duke of Anping, Fu, had a town of ten thousand households; institutions like Wei various kings.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhao held the title Prince of Jin he had Pei Xiu draft the revived five noble ranks; only Commandery Duke Fu of Anping kept a ten-thousand-household seat on the old Wei royal scale.

sentences.zh: 其餘縣公邑千八百戶，地方七十五里；

translations.literal: The rest: county dukes' towns one thousand eight hundred households, territory seventy-five li square;
translations.idiomatic: Other county dukes drew 1,800 households across seventy-five li square;

sentences.zh: 大國侯邑千六百戶，地方七十里；

translations.literal: Great-state marquises' towns one thousand six hundred households, territory seventy li square;
translations.idiomatic: Marquises of great kingdoms held 1,600 households over seventy li square;

sentences.zh: 次國侯邑千四百戶，地方六十五里；

translations.literal: Next-rank state marquises' towns one thousand four hundred households, territory sixty-five li square;
translations.idiomatic: Marquises of secondary kingdoms had 1,400 households and sixty-five li square;

sentences.zh: 大國伯邑千二百戶，地方六十里；

translations.literal: Great-state earls' towns one thousand two hundred households, territory sixty li square;
translations.idiomatic: Great-kingdom earls drew 1,200 households across sixty li;

sentences.zh: 次國伯邑千戶，地方五十五里；

translations.literal: Next-rank state earls' towns one thousand households, territory fifty-five li square;
translations.idiomatic: Lesser-kingdom earls had a thousand households over fifty-five li;

sentences.zh: 大國子邑八百戶，地方五十里；

translations.literal: Great-state viscounts' towns eight hundred households, territory fifty li square;
translations.idiomatic: Great-kingdom viscounts received eight hundred households in fifty li square;

sentences.zh: 次國子邑六百戶，地方四十五里；

translations.literal: Next-rank state viscounts' towns six hundred households, territory forty-five li square;
translations.idiomatic: Secondary viscounts held six hundred households over forty-five li;

sentences.zh: 男邑四百戶，地方四十里。

translations.literal: Barons' towns four hundred households, territory forty li square.
translations.idiomatic: Baronial seats stopped at four hundred households on forty li square.

sentences.zh: [5]武帝泰始元年，封諸王以郡爲國。

translations.literal: [5] In Jin Emperor Wu's first Taishi year, enfeoffed the various kings taking commanderies as states.
translations.idiomatic: [5] In the first year of Taishi Emperor Wu made each prince's domain a full commandery-sized kingdom.

sentences.zh: 邑二萬戶爲大國，置上中下三軍，兵五千人；

translations.literal: Towns twenty thousand households are a great state; establish upper, middle, and lower three armies—soldiers five thousand men;
translations.idiomatic: Twenty thousand households marked a great kingdom with upper, middle, and lower armies totaling five thousand troops;

sentences.zh: 邑萬戶爲次國，置上軍下軍，兵三千人；

translations.literal: Towns ten thousand households are a next-rank state; establish upper army and lower army—soldiers three thousand men;
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand households made a second-rank kingdom with upper and lower hosts of three thousand soldiers;

sentences.zh: 五千戶爲小國，置一軍，兵千五百人。

translations.literal: Five thousand households are a small state; establish one army—soldiers one thousand five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand households defined a small fief with a single army of fifteen hundred.

translations.literal: Kings did not go to their states; they served in office at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Princes were kept in the capital and never took up residence in their nominal kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 罷五等之制，公侯邑萬戶以上爲大國，五千戶以上爲次國，不滿五千戶爲小國。

translations.literal: Abolished the five-rank system: dukes and marquises' towns ten thousand households and above are great states; five thousand households and above are next-rank states; not filling five thousand households are small states.
translations.idiomatic: When the five-grade scheme was dropped, dukes and marquises above ten thousand households ranked as great fiefs, those above five thousand as middling, and the rest as small.

sentences.zh: 太康元年，平吳，大凡戶二百四十五萬九千八百四十，口一千六百一十六萬三千八百六十三。

translations.literal: Taikang first year, pacified Wu; in all households two million four hundred fifty-nine thousand eight hundred forty, mouths sixteen million one hundred sixty-three thousand eight hundred sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell in the first Taikang year the census added 2,459,840 households and 16,163,863 mouths to the Jin totals.

sentences.zh: 而江左諸國並三分食一，元帝渡江，太興元年，始制九分食一。

translations.literal: Moreover the various states east of the Jiang all together took one-third as food; Yuandi crossed the river; Taixing first year, first regulated one-ninth as food.
translations.idiomatic: Southern principalities had kept a third of their rent for the throne, but after Yuandi crossed the Yangzi the court in Taixing 1 cut the royal share to one-ninth.

translations.literal: Investigate the territory of Yuzhou in the Tribute of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: We now treat the ground classed as Yuzhou in the "Tribute of Yu."

sentences.zh: 及漢武帝，初置司隸校尉，所部三輔、三河諸郡。

translations.literal: Reaching Emperor Wu of Han, first established the Metropolitan Superintendent; what he administered: the Three Adjuncts, the Three Rivers commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu the Metropolitan Superintendent first appeared, overseeing the Three Adjuncts and Three Rivers commands.

sentences.zh: 其界西得雍州之京兆、馮翊、扶風三郡，北得冀州之河東、河內二郡，東得豫州之弘農、河南二郡，郡凡七。

translations.literal: Its boundary: west obtained Yongzhou's Jingzhao, Fengyi, Fufeng three commanderies; north obtained Jizhou's Hedong, Henei two commanderies; east obtained Yuzhou's Hongnong, Henan two commanderies—commanderies in all seven.
translations.idiomatic: Its span took Jingzhao, Fengyi, and Fufeng from Yongzhou in the west, Hedong and Henei from Ji in the north, and Hongnong and Henan from Yu in the east—seven commanderies in all.

sentences.zh: 位望隆于牧伯，[6]銀印青綬。

translations.literal: Position and outlook loftier than shepherds and regional lords, [6] silver seal, green ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: The post outranked provincial governors,[6] bearing a silver seal on green ribbon.

sentences.zh: 及光武都洛陽，司隸所部與前漢不異。

translations.literal: Reaching Guangwu's capital at Luoyang, what the Metropolitan Superintendent administered did not differ from Former Han.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangwu moved the capital to Luoyang the metropolitan belt matched Western Han's layout.

sentences.zh: 魏氏受禪，即都漢宮，司隸所部河南、河東、河內、弘農并冀州之平陽，合五郡，置司州。

translations.literal: The Wei house received abdication, immediately capital at Han palaces; what the Metropolitan Superintendent administered: Henan, Hedong, Henei, Hongnong, together with Jizhou's Pingyang—combined five commanderies, established Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei took the Han palaces at Luoyang, folded Henan, Hedong, Henei, Hongnong, and Pingyang from Ji into one metropolitan zone, and renamed it Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 晉仍居魏都，乃以三輔還屬雍州，分河南立滎陽，分雍州之京兆立上洛，廢東郡立頓丘，遂定名司州，以司隸校尉統之。

translations.literal: Jin still dwelt at Wei's capital; thereupon returned the Three Adjuncts to Yongzhou, split Henan to establish Yingyang, split Yongzhou's Jingzhao to establish Shangluo, abolished Dong commandery to establish Dunqiu, thereupon fixed the name Sizhou, with the Metropolitan Superintendent governing it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin stayed in Wei's Luoyang, sent the Three Adjuncts back to Yongzhou, peeled Yingyang from Henan and Shangluo from Jingzhao, replaced Dong with Dunqiu, and locked in the name Sizhou under the metropolitan commandant.

sentences.zh: 州統郡一十二，縣一百，戶四十七萬五千七百。

translations.literal: The province commands twelve commanderies, one hundred counties, households four hundred seventy-five thousand seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhou ruled twelve commanderies and a hundred counties with 475,700 registered households.

translations.idiomatic: [7] This marks editorial footnote seven in the source apparatus.

translations.idiomatic: Henan commandery

translations.idiomatic: 〈First set up under Han.

sentences.zh: 統縣十二，戶一十一萬四千四百。

translations.literal: Commands twelve counties, households one hundred eleven thousand four hundred.
translations.idiomatic: It governed twelve counties and 111,400 households.

translations.literal: Establishes a yin governor.〉
translations.idiomatic: Its capital seat held a metropolitan yin governor.〉

translations.idiomatic: Luoyang

translations.idiomatic: 〈The county had a captain of police.

translations.literal: Five wards, three markets.
translations.idiomatic: The city was divided into five wards and three market wards.

translations.literal: East-west seven li, north-south nine li.
translations.idiomatic: Its wall ran seven li east-west and nine li north-south.

sentences.zh: 東有建春、東陽、清明三門，南有開陽、平昌、宣陽、建陽四門，西有廣陽、西明、閶闔三門，北有大夏、廣莫二門。

translations.literal: East has three gates: Jianchun, Dongyang, Qingming; south has four gates: Kaiyang, Pingchang, Xuanyang, Jianyang; west has three gates: Guangyang, Ximing, Changhe; north has two gates: Daxia, Guangmo.
translations.idiomatic: East wall opened Jianchun, Dongyang, and Qingming; the south four gates including Kaiyang; the west Guangyang, Ximing, and Changhe; the north Daxia and Guangmo.

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉、河南尹及百官列城內也。〉

translations.literal: The Metropolitan Superintendent, Henan governor, and the hundred officials are arrayed within the city.〉
translations.idiomatic: The metropolitan commandant, the Henan governor, and the full bureaucracy sat inside those walls.〉

translations.idiomatic: Henan county

translations.idiomatic: 〈The Eastern Zhou royal city at Jia-Ru.〉

translations.literal: Gong
translations.idiomatic: Gong county

sentences.zh: 〈周孝王封周桓公孫惠公於鞏，號東周，故戰國時有東、西周號。

translations.literal: 〈King Xiao of Zhou enfeoffed Duke Hui of Zhou, grandson of Duke Huan of Zhou, at Gong, titled Eastern Zhou; therefore in Warring States times there were Eastern and Western Zhou titles.
translations.idiomatic: 〈King Xiao enfeoffed Duke Hui of Zhou at Gong as "Eastern Zhou," which is why Warring States texts speak of eastern and western Zhou polities.

translations.literal: Mount Mang and Shouyang are its boundary.〉
translations.idiomatic: Mount Mang and Shouyang marked its frontier.〉

sentences.zh: 秦兼天下，以爲三川、河東、南陽、潁川、碭、泗水、薛七郡。

translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao declared Zhao from Chang'an while his shepherds fanned out from Shanggui to Puban.

translations.literal: Shi Le captured Chang'an, again established Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le retook the city and revived the Yongzhou label.

sentences.zh: 石氏既敗，苻健僭據關中，又都長安，是爲前秦。

translations.literal: When the Shi house was defeated, Fu Jian usurped and held Guanzhong, again capital at Chang'an; this was Former Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian filled the vacuum after Shi's fall and made Chang'an the heart of Former Qin.

sentences.zh: 於是乃於雍州置司隸校尉，以豫州刺史鎮許昌，秦州刺史鎮上邽，荊州刺史鎮豐陽，洛州刺史鎮宜陽，并州刺史鎮蒲阪。

translations.literal: Thereupon on Yongzhou they set a Colonel Director of Retainers, using Yuzhou inspector at Xuchang, Qinzhou inspector at Shanggui, Jingzhou inspector at Fengyang, Luozhou inspector at Yiyang, Bingzhou inspector at Puban.
translations.idiomatic: He stacked a Sili colonel atop Yongzhou while inspectors watched Xuchang, Shanggui, Fengyang, Yiyang, and Puban.

sentences.zh: 苻堅時，分司隸爲雍州，分京兆爲咸陽郡，洛州刺史鎮陝城。

translations.literal: At Fu Jian's time, split Sili into Yongzhou, split Jingzhao into Xianyang commandery, Luozhou inspector at Shancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian peeled Sili into Yongzhou, carved Xianyang from Jingzhao, and parked Luozhou at Shancheng.

sentences.zh: 滅燕之後，分幽州置平州，鎮龍城，幽州刺史鎮薊城，河州刺史鎮枹罕，并州刺史鎮晉陽，豫州刺史鎮洛陽，兗州刺史鎮倉垣，雍州刺史鎮蒲阪。

translations.literal: After destroying Yan, split Youzhou to establish Pingzhou, garrisoned at Longcheng; Youzhou inspector at Ji; Hezhou inspector at Fuhan; Bingzhou inspector at Jinyang; Yuzhou inspector at Luoyang; Yanzhou inspector at Cangyuan; Yongzhou inspector at Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yan fell he added Pingzhou at Longcheng while a ring of inspectors held Ji, Fuhan, Jinyang, Luoyang, Cangyuan, and Puban.

sentences.zh: 於是移洛州居豐陽，以許昌置東豫州，以荊州刺史鎮襄陽，徐州刺史鎮彭城。

translations.literal: Thereupon moved Luozhou to Fengyang, used Xuchang to establish East Yuzhou, used Jingzhou inspector at Xiangyang, Xuzhou inspector at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He slid Luozhou south to Fengyang, opened East Yuzhou at Xuchang, and anchored Jing and Xu at Xiangyang and Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 既而姚萇滅苻氏，是爲後秦。

translations.literal: Soon Yao Chang destroyed the Fu house; this was Later Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang then swept away Former Qin to begin Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 及萇子興克洛陽，以并、冀二州牧鎮蒲阪，豫州牧鎮洛陽，兗州刺史鎮倉垣，分司隸領北五郡，置雍州刺史鎮安定。

translations.literal: When Chang's son Xing took Luoyang, using Bing and Ji two province shepherds at Puban, Yuzhou shepherd at Luoyang, Yanzhou inspector at Cangyuan, split Sili to oversee the northern five commanderies, established Yongzhou inspector at Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing pushed east until Bing and Ji answered from Puban while a new Yongzhou watched Anding.

sentences.zh: 及姚泓爲劉裕所滅，其地尋入赫連勃勃。

translations.literal: When Yao Hong was destroyed by Liu Yu, the land soon entered Helian Bobo.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu's conquest of Yao Hong handed the plateau to Helian Bobo within months.

sentences.zh: 勃勃僭號於統萬，是爲夏。

translations.literal: Bobo usurped the title at Tongwan; this was Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Bobo declared Xia from his Tongwan fortress.

sentences.zh: 置幽州牧於大城，又平劉義真於長安，遣子璝鎮焉，號曰南臺。

translations.literal: He set a Youzhou shepherd at Dacheng, and when he defeated Liu Yizhen at Chang'an, sent his son Gui to garrison it, called the South Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: He planted a Youzhou staff at Dacheng, crushed Liu Yizhen, and left his son Helian Gui holding a southern headquarters at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 以朔州牧鎮三城，秦州刺史鎮杏城，雍州刺史鎮陰密，并州刺史鎮蒲阪，梁州牧鎮安定，北秦州刺史鎮武功，豫州牧鎮李閏，[30]荊州刺史鎮陝，其州郡之名並不可知也。

translations.literal: Using Shuozhou shepherd at three cities, Qinzhou inspector at Xingcheng, Yongzhou inspector at Yinmi, Bingzhou inspector at Puban, Liangzhou shepherd at Anding, North Qinzhou inspector at Wugong, Yuzhou shepherd at Liwei, [30] Jingzhou inspector at Shan—the names of those provinces and commanderies are altogether unknowable.
translations.idiomatic: The roster lists Shuozhou at three forts, Qinzhou at Xingcheng, Yongzhou at Yinmi, Bing at Puban, Liang at Anding, north Qin at Wugong, Yu at Liwei, [30] Jing at Shan, yet many titles survive only as ghosts on the map.

sentences.zh: 然自元帝渡江，所置州亦皆遙領。

translations.literal: Yet from when Yuandi crossed the river, the provinces he set were also all held in absentia.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan crossed the Yangzi every northern title became a hollow commission held from the south.

sentences.zh: 初以魏該爲雍州刺史，鎮酇城，尋省，僑立始平郡，寄居武當城。

translations.literal: At first they made Wei Gai Yongzhou inspector at Zuo city, soon abolished, sojourning established Shiping commandery, lodging at Wudang fort.
translations.idiomatic: They first tried Wei Gai at Zuo, then papered Shiping onto Wudang when the seat vanished.

sentences.zh: 有秦國流人至江南，改堂邑爲秦郡，僑立尉氏縣屬焉。

translations.literal: There were Qin kingdom refugees who reached Jiangnan; they changed Tangyi to Qin commandery and sojourning established Weishi County belonging to it.
translations.idiomatic: Qin exiles persuaded the court to rename Tangyi Qin and hang a paper Weishi under it.

sentences.zh: 康帝時，庾翼爲荊州刺史，遷鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Kang, Yu Yi was Jingzhou inspector and moved the garrison to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Kang, Yu Yi shifted Jingzhou forward to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 其後秦雍流人多南出樊沔，孝武始於襄陽僑立雍州，仍立京兆、始平、扶風、河南、廣平、義成、北河南七郡，並屬襄陽。

translations.literal: Afterward Qin and Yong refugees mostly came south through Fan and Mian; Emperor Xiaowu first sojourning established Yongzhou at Xiangyang, still establishing Jingzhao, Shiping, Fufang, Henan, Guangping, Yicheng, and North Henan seven commanderies, all belonging to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu answered the Qin-Yong flood by pasting Yongzhou and seven paper commanderies onto Xiangyang.

translations.literal: Xiangyang formerly belonged to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang had lived under Jingzhou before the new stack.

sentences.zh: 案禹貢雍州之西界，周衰，其地爲狄。

translations.literal: Examining the Tribute of Yu, the western border of Yongzhou; when Zhou declined, its ground became Di.
translations.idiomatic: The classics draw Yongzhou's western rim here, later Di pasture once Zhou weakened.

sentences.zh: 秦興美陽甘泉宮，本匈奴鑄金人祭天之處。

translations.literal: Qin raised the Ganquan Palace at Meiyang; originally the place where the Xiongnu cast golden men to sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's Ganquan halls rose on Meiyang soil where the Xiongnu once poured bronze for heaven altars.

sentences.zh: 匈奴既失甘泉，又使休屠、渾邪王等居涼州之地。

translations.literal: When the Xiongnu lost Ganquan, they again had the Xiutu and Hunye kings dwell in Liangzhou ground.
translations.idiomatic: Losing Ganquan, the Xiongnu parked Xiutu and Hunye on the Liangzhou steppe.

sentences.zh: 二王後以地降漢，漢置張掖、酒泉、敦煌、武威郡。

translations.literal: After the two kings later surrendered the land to Han, Han established Zhangye, Jiuquan, Dunhuang, and Wuwei commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Han turned their pasture into Zhangye, Jiuquan, Dunhuang, and Wuwei once both kings yielded.

sentences.zh: 其後又置金城郡，謂之河西五郡。

translations.literal: Afterward again established Jincheng commandery; they called them the five Hexi commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Jincheng joined the list, giving the famous five west-of-the-river circuits.

sentences.zh: 漢改周之雍州爲涼州，蓋以地處西方，常寒涼也。

translations.literal: Han changed Zhou's Yongzhou to Liangzhou, probably because the ground lies in the west and is constantly cold and cool.
translations.idiomatic: Han swapped Yongzhou's old name for Liangzhou, hinting at the high cold air of the west.

sentences.zh: 地勢西北邪出，在南山之間，南隔西羌，西通西域，于時號爲斷匈奴右臂。

translations.literal: The terrain slants out northwest between southern ranges, south cut off from Western Qiang, west communicating with the Western Regions; at the time they called it severing the Xiongnu's right arm.
translations.idiomatic: The corridor angles northwest between ranges, walling off Qiang while opening toward the Tarim—Han called it the Xiongnu's severed right arm.

sentences.zh: 獻帝時，涼州數有亂，河西五郡去州隔遠，於是乃別以爲雍州。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xian's time Liangzhou repeatedly had turmoil; the five Hexi commanderies were distant from the province, thereupon separately made them Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han saw Liangzhou riot so often that the five western commanderies split off as their own Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 末又依古典定九州，乃合關右以爲雍州。

translations.literal: At the end again according to the classical nine provinces, then combined Guan you to make Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late Han realigned on the nine-provinces model and folded the Guanzhong west into Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 魏時復分以爲涼州，刺史領戊己校尉，護西域，如漢故事，至晉不改。

translations.literal: In Wei times again split it to make Liangzhou; the inspector led the gengji colonel and protected the Western Regions, like Han precedent, down to Jin unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Wei restored Liangzhou with an inspector-colonel pairing that guarded the Tarim as Han had done, and Jin kept the mold.

translations.idiomatic: Eight commanderies, forty-six counties, and thirty thousand seven hundred households stood on the books.

translations.idiomatic: 〈The Juyan marsh lies southeast, the "flowing sands" of the canon.〉

sentences.zh: 元康五年，惠帝分敦煌郡之宜禾、伊吾、冥安、深泉、廣至等五縣，分酒泉之沙頭縣，又別立會稽、新鄉，凡八縣爲晉昌郡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuankang, Emperor Hui split Yihe, Yiwu, Mingan, Shenquan, Guangzhi, the five counties of Dunhuang commandery, split Shatou county of Jiuquan, and separately established Kuaiji and Xinxiang, altogether eight counties as Jinchang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang five saw Hui peel five Dunhuang counties plus Jiuquan's Shatou and two new names into Jinchang commandery.

sentences.zh: 永寧中，張軌爲涼州刺史，鎮武威，上表請合秦雍流移人於姑臧西北，置武興郡，統武興、大城、烏支、襄武、晏然、新鄣、平狄、司監等縣。

translations.literal: In Yongning, Zhang Gui was Liangzhou inspector, garrisoned at Wuwei; he submitted a memorial asking to gather Qin and Yong displaced persons northwest of Guzang and establish Wuxing commandery, governing Wuxing, Dacheng, Wuzhi, Xiangwu, Yanran, Xinzhang, Pingdi, Sijian, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Yongning-era Zhang Gui asked to pack Qin-Yong refugees northwest of Guzang into a new Wuxing commandery with nine satellite counties.

sentences.zh: 又分西平界置晉興郡，統晉興、枹罕、永固、臨津、臨鄣、廣昌、大夏、遂興、罕唐、左南等縣。

translations.literal: Again split Xiping's border to establish Jinxing commandery, governing Jinxing, Fohan, Yonggu, Linjin, Linzhang, Guangchang, Daxia, Suixing, Hantang, Zuonan, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: He also shaved Xiping to raise Jinxing with a string of paper counties from Fohan to Zuonan.

sentences.zh: 是時中原淪沒，元帝徙居江左，軌乃控據河西，稱晉正朔，是爲前涼。

translations.literal: At this time the Central Plain was lost; Yuandi moved to live east of the river; Gui then controlled Hexi, called himself Jin's orthodox calendar; this was Former Liang.
translations.idiomatic: While Yuan ruled from the left bank, Zhang Gui held the Hexi corridor in Jin's name—the state later called Former Liang.

sentences.zh: 及張寔，分金城之令居、枝陽二縣，又立永登縣，合三縣立廣武郡。

translations.literal: When it came to Zhang Shi, he split Lingju and Zhiyang, two counties of Jincheng, and also established Yongdeng County, combining three counties to establish Guangwu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi carved Lingju and Zhiyang from Jincheng, added Yongdeng, and chartered Guangwu over the three.

sentences.zh: 張茂分武興、金城、西平、安故爲定州。

translations.literal: Zhang Mao divided Wuxing, Jincheng, Xiping, and Angu into Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao tried to anchor Dingzhou on Wuxing, Jincheng, Xiping, and Angu.

sentences.zh: 張駿分武威、武興、西平、張掖、酒泉、建康、西海、西郡、湟河、晉興、廣武合十一郡爲涼州，[34]興晉、金城、武始、南安、永晉、大夏、武成、漢中爲河州，敦煌、晉昌、高昌、西域都護、戊己校尉、玉門大護軍三郡三營爲沙州。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun split Wuwei, Wuxing, Xiping, Zhangye, Jiuquan, Jiankang, Xihai, Xijun, Huanghe, Jinxing, and Guangwu—altogether eleven commanderies—as Liangzhou, [34] Xingjin, Jincheng, Wushi, Nan'an, Yongjin, Daxia, Wucheng, and Hanzhong as Hezhou, Dunhuang, Jinchang, Gaochang, Western Regions protector, gengji colonel, and Yumen grand protector—three commanderies and three camps—as Shazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun reorganized the west into Liangzhou on eleven bases [34], stacked a parallel Hezhou on the Hanzhong rim, and spun Shazhou from Dunhuang, the Tarim staff, and the desert protectorates.

translations.literal: [35] Zhang Jun acting Liangzhou area commander held three provinces.
translations.idiomatic: [35] Jun held concurrent authority as Liangzhou commander-in-chief over three circuits.

sentences.zh: 張祚又以敦煌郡爲商州。

translations.literal: Zhang Zuo again used Dunhuang commandery as Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo rebranded Dunhuang as Shangzhou on his maps.

sentences.zh: 永興中，置漢陽縣以守牧地，張玄靚改爲祁連郡。

translations.literal: In Yongxing, they established Hanyang County to guard pasture ground; Zhang Xuanjing changed it to Qilian commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing saw a Hanyang garrison county that Xuanjing promoted into Qilian commandery.

translations.literal: Zhang Tianxi separately established Linsong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi added another Linsong commandery atop the pile.

sentences.zh: 天錫降於苻氏，其地尋爲呂光所據。

translations.literal: When Tianxi surrendered to the Fu house, the land soon was held by Lü Guang.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianxi yielded to Fu Jian, Lü Guang seized the corridor almost at once.

sentences.zh: 呂光都於姑臧後，以郭黁言讖，改昌松爲東張掖郡。

translations.literal: After Lü Guang made his capital at Guzang, because of Guo Qin's prophecy verse, changed Changsong to East Zhangye commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang, settled at Guzang, renamed Changsong East Zhangye on Guo Qin's omen talk.

sentences.zh: 及呂隆降於姚興，其地三分。

translations.literal: When Lü Long surrendered to Yao Xing, the land was split three ways.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Long's capitulation to Later Qin shattered the plateau into three rival states.

sentences.zh: 武昭王爲西涼，建號於敦煌。

translations.literal: Prince Zhaowu was Western Liang, establishing title at Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao's Western Liang began from Dunhuang with the Zhaowu princely title.

sentences.zh: 禿髮烏孤爲南涼，建號於樂都。

translations.literal: Tufa Wugu was Southern Liang, establishing title at Ledu.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Wugu declared Southern Liang from Ledu.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜爲北涼，建號於張掖。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun was Northern Liang, establishing title at Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun styled his realm Northern Liang with a seat at Zhangye.

translations.literal: Yet they divided and held the five Hexi commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Each faction still clutched pieces of the five Hexi basins.

sentences.zh: 案禹貢本雍州之域，魏始分隴右置焉，刺史領護羌校尉，中間暫廢。

translations.literal: Examining the Tribute of Yu, it was originally Yongzhou territory; Wei first split Longyou to establish it; the inspector led the Protect Qiang Colonel; in the middle briefly abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The classics file this strip under Yongzhou until Wei split Longyou, paired it with a Qiang colonel, and once briefly dropped the office.

sentences.zh: 及泰始五年，又以雍州隴右五郡及涼州之金城、梁州之陰平，合七郡置秦州，鎮冀城。

translations.literal: When it came to the fifth year of Taishi, again using five Longyou commanderies of Yongzhou and Jincheng of Liangzhou, Yinping of Liangzhou—seven commanderies combined—established Qinzhou, garrisoned at Jicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi five merged five Longyou circuits with Jincheng and Yinping into Qinzhou headquartered at Jicheng.

sentences.zh: 太康三年，罷秦州，并雍州。

translations.idiomatic: Taikang three folded Qinzhou back into Yongzhou.

translations.literal: In the seventh year, again established, garrisoned at Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang seven revived it with a seat at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 張駿分屬涼州，又以狄道縣立武始郡。

translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun reassigned the belt to Liangzhou and raised Wushi from Didao county.

sentences.zh: 江左分梁爲秦，寄居梁州，又立氐池爲北秦州。

translations.literal: East of the river split Liang to make Qin, sojourning lodged in Liangzhou, again established Chichi as North Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 案禹貢華陽黑水之地，舜置十二牧，則其一也。

translations.literal: Examining the Tribute of Yu, the land of Huayang and the black water; Shun established twelve herds—this is one of them.
translations.idiomatic: The Huayang–Heishui belt was one of Shun's twelve pastorates in the canon.

sentences.zh: 梁者，言西方金剛之氣強梁，故因名焉。

translations.literal: Liang means speaking of the western metal-gang qi being strong beam; therefore took the name from it.
translations.idiomatic: The name Liang evokes hard western metal qi, harsh as a beam, hence the label.

translations.idiomatic: The Zhouli survey paired Liang with Yong on one chart.

sentences.zh: 漢不立州名，以其地爲益州。

translations.literal: Han did not establish a province name; took its land as Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han simply filed the whole basin under Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 及獻帝初平六年，[38]以臨江縣屬永寧郡。

translations.literal: When it came to the sixth year of Emperor Xian's Chuping, [38] attached Linjiang County to Yongning commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chuping six attached Linjiang to Yongning commandery [38].

sentences.zh: 建安六年，劉璋改永寧爲巴東郡，分巴郡墊江置巴西郡。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jian'an, Liu Zhang changed Yongning to Badong commandery, split Ba commandery's Dianjiang to establish Baxi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jian'an six saw Liu Zhang retitle Yongning Badong and spin Baxi from Ba's Dianjiang.

sentences.zh: 劉備據蜀，又分廣漢之葭萌、涪城、梓潼、白水四縣，改葭萌曰漢壽，又立漢德縣，以爲梓潼郡；

translations.literal: Liu Bei holding Shu again split Jiameng, Fucheng, Zitong, and Baishui, four counties of Guanghan, changed Jiameng to Hanshou, again established Hande County, making Zitong commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei carved Zitong from Guanghan, renamed Jiameng Hanshou, added Hande, and framed a new Zitong commandery;

sentences.zh: 割巴郡之宕渠、宣漢、漢昌三縣置宕渠郡，尋省，以縣並屬巴西郡。

translations.literal: Liu Bei cut Dangqu, Xuanyuan, and Hanchang three counties of Ba commandery to establish Dangqu commandery, soon abolished, merging counties all belonging to Baxi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei briefly raised Dangqu from three Ba counties, then folded everything back into Baxi.

sentences.zh: 泰始三年，分益州，立梁州於漢中，改漢壽爲晉壽，又分廣漢置新都郡。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taishi, split Yizhou, established Liangzhou at Hanzhong, changed Hanshou to Jinshou, again split Guanghan to establish Xindu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi three created Liangzhou at Hanzhong, rechristened Hanshou Jinshou, and cut Xindu from Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 惠帝復分巴西置宕渠郡，統宕渠、漢昌、宣漢三縣，并以新城、魏興、上庸合四郡以屬梁州。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui again split Baxi to establish Dangqu commandery, governing Dangqu, Hanchang, and Xuanyuan three counties, and together with Xincheng, Weixing, and Shangyong combined four commanderies to belong to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hui re-cut Dangqu from Baxi and stacked Xincheng, Weixing, and Shangyong under Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋而梁州郡縣沒于李特，永嘉中又分屬楊茂搜，其晉人流寓於梁益者，仍於二州立南北二陰平郡。

translations.literal: Soon Liangzhou commanderies and counties were lost to Li Te; in Yongjia again split to belong to Yang Maosou; those Jin people drifting in Liang and Yi, still on the two provinces established south and north Yinping commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou collapsed to Li Te, Yongjia refugees bowed to Yang Maosou, and exiles pasted twin Yinping commanderies onto Liang and Yi.

sentences.zh: 及桓溫平蜀之後，以巴漢流人立晉昌郡，領長樂、安晉、延壽、安樂、宣漢、寧都、新興、吉陽、東關、永安十縣；

translations.literal: When Huan Wen pacified Shu afterward, using Ba-Han refugees established Jinchang commandery, overseeing Changle, Anjin, Yanshou, Anle, Xuanyuan, Ningdu, Xinxing, Jiyang, Dongguan, Yongan ten counties;
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Wen took Shu he chartered Jinchang for Ba-Han refugees with ten nominal counties;

sentences.zh: 又置益昌、晉興二縣，屬巴西郡；

translations.literal: again established Yichang and Jinxing two counties, belonging to Baxi commandery;
translations.idiomatic: then added Yichang and Jinxing under Baxi;

sentences.zh: 於德陽界東南置遂寧郡；

translations.literal: On the southeast of the Deyang border they established Suining commandery;
translations.idiomatic: They chartered Suining southeast of the Deyang frontier;

sentences.zh: 又於晉壽置劍閣縣，屬梁州。

translations.literal: Again at Jinshou established Jiange County, belonging to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court pasted Jiange County onto Jinshou under Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 後孝武分梓潼北界立晉壽郡，統晉壽、白水、邵歡、興安四縣；

translations.literal: Later Emperor Xiaowu split the northern border of Zitong to establish Jinshou commandery, governing Jinshou, Baishui, Shaohuan, and Xing'an four counties;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu carved Jinshou commandery from northern Zitong with four counties;

sentences.zh: 梓潼郡徙居梓潼，罷劍閣縣；

translations.literal: Zitong commandery moved its seat to Zitong, abolished Jiange County;
translations.idiomatic: The Zitong seat shifted onto the old Zitong town and Jiange county vanished;

sentences.zh: 又別置南漢中郡，分巴西、梓潼爲金山郡。

translations.literal: again separately established South Hanzhong commandery, split Baxi and Zitong to make Jinshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: then invented South Hanzhong and Jinshan by splitting Baxi and Zitong.

sentences.zh: 及安帝時，又立新巴、汶陽二郡，又有北新巴、華陽、南陰平、北陰平四郡，其後又立巴渠、懷安、宋熙、白水、上洛、北上洛、南宕渠、懷漢、新興、安康等十郡。

translations.literal: When it came to Emperor An's time, again established Xinba and Wenyang two commanderies, and also had North Xinba, Huayang, South Yinping, North Yinping four commanderies; afterward again established Baqu, Huai'an, Songxi, Baishui, Shangluo, North Shangluo, South Dangqu, Huaihan, Xinxing, Ankang and so on ten commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: An's reign piled on Xinba, Wenyang, twin Yinping circuits, and a raft of paper commanderies from Baqu to Ankang.

sentences.zh: 案禹貢及舜十二牧俱爲梁州之域，周合梁於雍，則又爲雍州之地。

translations.literal: Examining the Tribute of Yu and Shun's twelve herds, both are Liangzhou territory; Zhou merged Liang with Yong, then again became Yongzhou ground.
translations.idiomatic: Classics call it Liangzhou under Shun, yet Zhou folded Liang into Yong before Han re-split the names.

sentences.zh: 《春秋元命包》云：「參伐流爲益州，益之爲言阨也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Yuanming Bao says: "Shen and Fa flowing become Yizhou; yi as word means blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanming Bao glosses Yizhou from the Shen-Fa stars and the word yi, blocked.

sentences.zh: 」言其所在之地險阨也，亦曰疆壤益大，故以名焉。

translations.literal: " Speaking of its place being dangerous and blocked; also saying the border soil grew ever vaster, therefore used the name.
translations.idiomatic: It hints at sheer cliffs and widening frontiers—hence the label yi.

sentences.zh: 始秦惠王滅蜀，置郡，以張若爲蜀守。

translations.literal: At first King Hui of Qin destroyed Shu, established commanderies, making Zhang Ruo Shu governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Huiwang annexed Shu he set up commanderies under Zhang Ruo.

sentences.zh: 及始皇置三十六郡，蜀郡之名不改。

translations.literal: When it came to the First Emperor establishing thirty-six commanderies, the name Shu commandery was not changed.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang's thirty-six circuits still called the core Shu.

translations.literal: In Han's beginning there were Hanzhong, Ba, and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Early Han counted Hanzhong, Ba, and Shu.

sentences.zh: 高祖六年，分蜀置廣漢，凡爲四郡。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Gaozu, split Shu to establish Guanghan; altogether became four commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu six added Guanghan to make four western commanderies.

sentences.zh: 武帝開西南夷，更置犍爲、牂柯、越巂、益州四郡，凡八郡，遂置益州統焉，益州蓋始此也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu opened the southwestern Yi, further established Qianwei, Zangke, Yuegui, and Yizhou four commanderies; altogether eight commanderies, then established Yizhou to oversee them; Yizhou probably began here.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi's Yi campaigns added Qianwei, Zangke, Yuegui, and Yizhou circuits, then an Yizhou inspector over eight commands—the name starts here.

sentences.zh: 及後漢，明帝以新附置永昌郡，安帝又以諸道置蜀、廣漢、犍爲三郡屬國都尉，及靈帝又以汶江、蠶陵、廣柔三縣立汶山郡。

translations.literal: When it came to Later Han, Emperor Ming because newly attached established Yongchang commandery; Emperor An again because various roads established Shu, Guanghan, and Qianwei three dependent-state colonels; when it came to Emperor Ling again used Wenjiang, Canling, and Guangrou three counties to establish Wenshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han layered Yongchang, three dependent-state offices, and Emperor Ling's Wenshan carve-out.

sentences.zh: 獻帝初平元年，劉璋分巴郡立永寧郡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Xian's Chuping, Liu Zhang split Ba commandery to establish Yongning commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chuping one saw Liu Zhang peel Yongning from Ba.

sentences.zh: [42]建安六年，改永寧爲巴東，以巴郡爲巴西，又立涪陵郡。

translations.literal: [42] In the sixth year of Jian'an, changed Yongning to Badong, used Ba commandery as Baxi, again established Fuling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: [42] Jian'an six retitled Yongning Badong, swapped Baxi for Ba, and added Fuling.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，劉備分巴郡立固陵郡。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, Liu Bei split Ba commandery to establish Guling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jian'an twenty-one had Liu Bei raise Guling from Ba.

sentences.zh: 蜀章武元年又改固陵爲巴東郡，巴西郡爲巴郡，又分廣漢立梓潼郡，分犍爲立江陽郡，以蜀郡屬國爲漢嘉郡，以犍爲屬國爲朱提郡。

translations.literal: Shu Zhangwu first year again changed Guling to Badong commandery, Baxi commandery to Ba commandery, again split Guanghan to establish Zitong commandery, split Qianwei to establish Jiangyang commandery, used Shu dependent state as Hanjia commandery, used Qianwei dependent state as Zhuti commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei's Zhangwu edicts renamed Guling, flipped Baxi back to Ba, and spun Zitong, Jiangyang, Hanjia, and Zhuti.

sentences.zh: 劉禪建興二年，改益州郡爲建寧郡，廣漢屬國爲陰平郡，分建寧永昌立雲南郡，分建寧牂柯立興古郡，分廣漢立東廣漢郡。

translations.literal: Liu Shan Jianxing second year changed Yizhou commandery to Jianning commandery, Guanghan dependent state to Yinping commandery, split Jianning and Yongchang to establish Yunnan commandery, split Jianning and Zangke to establish Xinggu commandery, split Guanghan to establish East Guanghan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shan's Jianxing two retitled Yizhou Jianning, peeled Yunnan and Xinggu, and cloned East Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 魏景元中，蜀平，省東廣漢郡。

translations.literal: In Wei's Jingyuan middle, Shu was pacified, abolished East Guanghan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wei struck East Guanghan once Shu surrendered.

sentences.zh: 及武帝泰始二年，分益州置梁州，以漢中屬焉。

translations.literal: When it came to Emperor Wu's second year of Taishi, split Yizhou to establish Liangzhou, attaching Hanzhong to it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Wudi's Taishi two carved Liangzhou from Yizhou and took Hanzhong with it.

translations.literal: In the seventh year, again split Yizhou to establish Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi seven added Ningzhou as another slice of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 惠帝之後，李特僭號於蜀，稱漢，益州郡縣皆沒于特。

translations.literal: After Emperor Hui, Li Te usurped the title in Shu, called Han; Yizhou commanderies and counties all sank into Te.
translations.idiomatic: Post-Hui Li Te styled himself Han and swallowed every Yizhou seat.

sentences.zh: 李雄又分漢嘉、蜀二郡立沈黎、漢原二郡。

translations.literal: Li Xiong again split Hanjia and Shu two commanderies to establish Shenli and Hanyuan two commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong cut Shenli and Hanyuan from Hanjia and Shu.

sentences.zh: 是時益州郡縣雖沒李氏，江左並遙置之。

translations.literal: At this time although Yizhou commanderies and counties were lost to the Li house, east of the river they all held them in absentia.
translations.idiomatic: Even while Li held the soil, Jiankang kept ghost registers for the same names.

sentences.zh: 桓溫滅蜀，其地復爲晉有，省漢原、沈黎而立南陰平、晉原、寧蜀、始寧四郡焉。

translations.literal: When Huan Wen destroyed Shu, the land again became Jin's; abolished Hanyuan and Shenli and established South Yinping, Jinyuan, Ningshu, and Shining four commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's conquest restored Jin names, trading Shenli and Hanyuan for four new southern circuits.

sentences.zh: 咸安二年，益州復沒於苻氏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xian'an, Yizhou again was lost to the Fu house.
translations.idiomatic: Xian'an two handed Yizhou back to Former Qin.

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taiyuan, again became Jin's.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan eight returned the basin to Eastern Jin.

sentences.zh: 隆安二年，又立晉熙、遂寧、晉寧三郡云。

translations.literal: In the second year of Long'an, again established Jinxi, Suining, and Jinning three commanderies, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Long'an two reportedly added Jinxi, Suining, and Jinning.

translations.literal: In Han and Wei it was Yizhou territory.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei filed this block under Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 泰始七年，武帝以益州地廣，分益州之建寧、興古、雲南、交州之永昌，合四郡爲寧州，統縣四十五，戶八萬三千。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taishi, Emperor Wu because Yizhou ground was vast, split Jianning, Xinggu, Yunnan of Yizhou and Yongchang of Jiao—four commanderies combined—to make Ningzhou, governing forty-five counties, households eighty-three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi seven saw Wudi spin Ningzhou from four southern commanderies with forty-five counties and eighty-three thousand households.

translations.idiomatic: Yunnan commandery.

translations.idiomatic: Nine counties counted ninety-two hundred households.〉

translations.literal: Yunping Yunnan Longdong Qingling Gufu Xielong Dieyu Suijiu Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: Yunping, Yunnan, Longdong, Qingling, Gufu, Xielong, Dieyu, Suijiu, and Yongning counties.

translations.idiomatic: Xinggu commandery.

translations.idiomatic: Jianning commandery.

translations.idiomatic: Seventeen counties counted twenty-nine thousand households.〉

translations.literal: Wei Kunze Cunxie Xinding Tangao Mudan Tonglai Loujiang Muma Guchang Lianran Qinzang Shuangbai Yuyuan Xiuyun Lingqiu Dianchi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, Kunze, Cunxie, Xinding, Tangao, Mudan, Tonglai, Loujiang, Muma, Guchang, Lianran, Qinzang, Shuangbai, Yuyuan, Xiuyun, Lingqiu, and Dianchi counties.

translations.idiomatic: Yongchang commandery.

translations.literal: Buwei Yongshou Bisu Yongxiang Nanfu Xitang Ailao Bonan.
translations.idiomatic: Buwei, Yongshou, Bisu, Yongxiang, Nanfu, Xitang, Ailao, and Bonan counties.

sentences.zh: 太康三年，武帝又廢寧州入益州，立南夷校尉以護之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taikang, Emperor Wu again abolished Ningzhou into Yizhou, established South Yi Colonel to protect it.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang three merged Ningzhou back into Yizhou and posted a South Yi colonel.

sentences.zh: 太安二年，惠帝復置寧州，又分建寧以西七縣別立爲益州郡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tai'an, Emperor Hui again established Ningzhou, again split seven counties west of Jianning separately to establish Yizhou commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Tai'an two revived Ningzhou and peeled a new Yizhou commandery from western Jianning.

sentences.zh: 永嘉二年，改益州郡曰晉寧，分牂柯立平夷、夜郎二郡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongjia, changed Yizhou commandery to Jinning, split Zangke to establish Pingyi and Yelang two commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjia two retitled Yizhou Jinning and added Pingyi and Yelang from Zangke.

translations.literal: [47] Yet at this time the ground again was held by Li Te.
translations.idiomatic: [47] Li Te seized the same ground almost immediately afterward.

sentences.zh: 其後李壽分寧州興古、永昌、雲南、朱提、越巂、河陽六郡爲漢州。

translations.literal: Afterward Li Shou split Xinggu, Yongchang, Yunnan, Zhuti, Yuegui, and Heyang six commanderies of Ningzhou as Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou later declared Hanzhou over six southern commanderies.

sentences.zh: 咸康四年，分牂柯、夜郎、朱提、越巂四郡置安州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xiankang, split Zangke, Yelang, Zhuti, and Yuegui four commanderies to establish Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiankang four chartered Anzhou from four Zangke rim counties.

sentences.zh: 八年，又罷并寧州，以越巂還屬益州，省永昌郡焉。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, again abolished and merged into Ningzhou, returning Yuegui to belong to Yizhou, abolishing Yongchang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiankang eight folded Anzhou back, returned Yuegui to Yizhou, and struck Yongchang.

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Editorial collation notes.

sentences.zh: 崆山訪道「崆」，宋本、局本等作「風」，殿本作「崆」，今從殿本。

translations.literal: For Kongshan visiting the Way, "Kong": Song and bureau editions etc. write "wind"; the palace edition writes "Kong"; now follow the palace edition.
translations.idiomatic: The graph for Kongshan varies: Song and bureau prints read "wind" where the palace block reads Kong, which this edition follows.

sentences.zh: 黃帝于崆峒山訪道，傳自莊子。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor visiting the Way on Kongtong Mountain is transmitted from Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor's Kongtong visit comes down from Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 義陽據下「武帝增置」之文及「義陽郡」下之文，義陽郡又置于晉武帝太康時。

translations.literal: Regarding Yiyang: according to the text below "Emperor Wu additionally established" and the text under "Yiyang commandery," Yiyang commandery was again placed in Emperor Wu of Jin's Taikang period.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyang's Jin placement aligns with the "Wudi added" line and the Yiyang commandery entry under Taikang.

sentences.zh: 永壽三年戶千六十七萬七千九百六十口五千六百四十八萬六千八百五十六後漢書郡國志在本志校記中以後簡稱《續漢志·一》注云：「永壽二年，戶千六百七萬九百六，口五千六萬六千八百五十六人。」

translations.literal: Yongshou third year households one thousand sixty-seven thousand seven hundred ninety, mouths five thousand six hundred forty-eight thousand six hundred fifty-six; in the Treatise on Commanderies of Later Han Book, in this treatise's collation notes hereafter abbreviated "Continuation Han Treatise I" note says: "Yongshou second year, households one thousand six hundred seven thousand nine hundred six, mouths five thousand six ten thousand six thousand eight hundred fifty-six persons."
translations.idiomatic: The main text's Yongshou 3 tally clashes with Li Xian's note citing Yongshou 2 figures in the continuation treatise—editors flag the mismatch.

sentences.zh: 嗣王之庶子爲亭侯各本無「亭」字，殿本有。

translations.literal: The secondary sons of enfeoffed kings as district marquis: various editions lack the word "district"; the palace edition has it.
translations.idiomatic: Some prints omit "district" before district marquis; the palace block restores it.

sentences.zh: 今從殿本，與魏志文帝紀合。

translations.literal: Now follow the palace edition, matching the Wei Annals Wendi chapter.
translations.idiomatic: We follow the palace reading to match Wei Records, Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 位望隆于牧伯「隆」，各本作「降」，宋本作「隆」，今從宋本。

translations.literal: Rank and eminence higher than shepherds and earls: "eminence," various editions write "descend"; Song edition writes "eminence"; now follow Song edition.
translations.idiomatic: One line reads rank "higher than" governors, not "descended from" them, following the Song imprint.

sentences.zh: 縣一百戶四十七萬五千七百下所列爲縣九十九，戶四十九萬二千四百。

translations.literal: One hundred counties, households four hundred seventy-five thousand seven hundred: below listed are ninety-nine counties, households four hundred ninety-two thousand four hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The stated hundred counties and 475,700 households do not match the ninety-nine counties and 492,400 households tabulated below.

sentences.zh: 兩數不合，各州頗有此類情況，以後不具校。

translations.literal: The two figures do not match; each province often has this kind of situation; hereafter not fully collated.
translations.idiomatic: Editors note such mismatches recur by province and are not exhaustively reconciled hereafter.

sentences.zh: 有博浪長沙張良擊秦始皇處 畢沅《晉書·地理志·新補正》

translations.literal: On Bolangsha where Zhang Liang struck the First Emperor of Qin: Bi Yuan, New Corrections to the Jinshu Treatise on Geography
translations.idiomatic: Collation on Bolangsha: Bi Yuan's supplement to the Jinshu geography treatise

translations.literal: (hereafter abbreviated "Bi Coll.")
translations.idiomatic: (hereafter cited as the Bi Coll.)

sentences.zh: 謂「遍檢諸地志，皆云博浪沙在陽武。

translations.literal: States: "Searching all gazetteers, all say Bolangsha is in Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Bi argues every gazetteer places Bolangsha in Yangwu.

sentences.zh: 」疑此十二字注本在「陽武」下，錯簡入卷縣耳。

translations.literal: " Suspect these twelve characters of commentary originally stood under "Yangwu," wrongly slipped into the Juan county line.
translations.idiomatic: Editors suspect a misplaced gloss that belonged under Yangwu drifted into the Juan county entry.

sentences.zh: 分京兆南部置「部」，各本作「郡」，宋本作「部」，今從宋本。

translations.literal: Splitting the southern part of Jingzhao to establish "bu": various editions write "commandery"; Song edition writes "bu"; now follow Song edition.
translations.idiomatic: The particle after splitting southern Jingzhao should read "bu" per the Song block, not "commandery."

sentences.zh: 汾陽公國相 《畢校》及方愷《新校·晉書·地理志》

translations.literal: Fenyang ducal chancellor: Bi Coll. and Fang Kai's New Collation of the Jinshu Treatise on Geography
translations.idiomatic: Headnote on Fenyang ducal staff citing Bi Yuan and Fang Kai.

translations.literal: (hereafter abbreviated "Fang Coll.")
translations.idiomatic: (Hereafter cited as the Fang Coll.)

translations.literal: both state that "Fenyang" ought to be "Fenyin."
translations.idiomatic: Both collations argue the graph should read Fenyin, not Fenyang.

sentences.zh: 按：「公國相」，各本作「公相國」，「相國」二字誤倒，宋本不誤，今從宋本。

translations.literal: Note: "ducal chancellor," various editions write "duke chancellor," two characters inverted in error; Song edition is not wrong; now follow Song edition.
translations.idiomatic: Song prints keep "ducal chancellor" while others accidentally transpose "chancellor duke."

sentences.zh: 清泉考異：本「清淵」，避唐諱改。

translations.literal: Qingquan textual note: originally "Qingyuan," changed to avoid Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Qingquan was Qingyuan until Tang editors dodged a homophone taboo.

sentences.zh: 大戚考異：大戚即廣戚，隋避煬帝諱改。

translations.literal: Daq textual note: Daq is Guangqi, changed to avoid Sui Yangdi taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Daq is the old Guangqi label, tweaked under Sui naming taboos.

sentences.zh: 兗端也「端」，各本作「瑞」，今從宋本作「端」。

translations.literal: Yan "upright": various editions write "auspicious"; now follow Song edition writing "upright."
translations.idiomatic: The gloss word should read "upright," not the swapped "auspicious," per Song.

sentences.zh: 魏武帝封考異：袁廷檮曰，「武帝」當作「元帝」，即常道鄉公也。

translations.literal: Wei Wudi enfeoffment textual note: Yuan Tingtao says "Wudi" should be "Yuandi," i.e., the Duke of Changdao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tingtao argues the fief line should name Cao Huan as Yuandi, not Cao Cao.

translations.literal: When Jin received the abdication, he was enfeoffed King of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: The last Wei ruler became king of Chenliu once Jin took the mandate.

translations.literal: Jiyin commandery originally wrote "Jiyang commandery."
translations.idiomatic: The block wrongly headed Jiyang instead of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 考異：漢無濟陽郡，蓋「濟陰」之誤。

translations.literal: Textual note: Han had no Jiyang commandery; probably error for "Jiyin."
translations.idiomatic: Han never chartered Jiyang on this ground; Jiyin is the intended name.

sentences.zh: 卞壺傳濟陰冤句人，宋書州郡志於城武、離狐二縣並云晉太康地志屬濟陰。

translations.literal: Bi Kun's biography calls him a Yuanyuan man of Jiyin; Song Treatise on Commanderies at Chengwu and Ligou counties both say Jin Taikang land treatise listed them under Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies and the Song commandery treatise tie Yuanyuan to Jiyin, not Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 按：《左傳》隱公七年杜注及郤詵傳並可證。

translations.literal: Note: Zuo Duke Yin seventh year Du's commentary and Xi Shen's biography alike confirm it.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo tradition and Jin texts both anchor the reading.

translations.literal: Now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The edition adopts that correction.

sentences.zh: 宛句卞壺傳作「冤句」，《漢書·地理志》在本志校記中以後簡稱漢志上、《續漢志·三》、宋書州郡志在本志校記中以後簡稱宋志一、魏書地形志在本志校記中以後簡稱後魏志二、隋書地理志在本志校記中以後簡稱隋志中並作「冤句」。

translations.literal: Wanqu: Bi Kun's biography writes "Yuanqu"; Han Treatise on Geography in this treatise's collation notes hereafter abbreviated Han Treatise I, Continuation Han Treatise III, Song Treatise on Commanderies hereafter abbreviated Song Treatise I, Wei Treatise on Terrain hereafter abbreviated Later Wei Treatise II, Sui Treatise on Geography hereafter abbreviated Sui Treatise middle, all write "Yuanqu."
translations.idiomatic: Every major gazetteer spells the county Yuanqu, not Wanqu, citing Han through Sui parallels.

translations.literal: Hulu originally wrote "Luhu."
translations.idiomatic: The name Hulu was reversed as Luhu in some blocks.

sentences.zh: 舉正：當作「湖陸」，見《左傳》襄公十九年杜注。

translations.literal: Correction: should be "Hulu," see Zuo Duke Xiang nineteenth year Du's commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Xiang 19 Du preface fixes the Hulu order.

sentences.zh: 斠注：水經濟水、泗水注亦作「湖陸」。

translations.literal: Commentary note: Shuijing notes on Ji and Si rivers likewise write "Hulu."
translations.idiomatic: Li Daoyuan's Shuijing agrees on Hulu.

sentences.zh: 按：漢志上、《續漢志·三》謂本曰湖陵，莽改湖陸。

translations.literal: Note: Han Treatise I and Continuation Han Treatise III say originally called Huling, Wang changed to Hulu.
translations.idiomatic: Han registers show Wang Mang retitled Huling to Hulu.

translations.literal: Now corrected by transposition.
translations.idiomatic: Editors swap the graphs to match sources.

sentences.zh: 烏下聚馬與龍晉書地理志注後簡稱馬校：「烏」當作「嶲」。

translations.literal: Wuxia hamlet: Ma and Long Jinshu geography commentary hereafter abbreviated Ma Coll.: "crow" should be "Gui."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ju-long argues the first character should read Gui, not crow.

sentences.zh: 《續漢志·三》作「嶲下聚」，劉昭注引《左傳》僖公二十六年杜注作「嶲下」。

translations.literal: Continuation Han Treatise III writes "Guixia hamlet"; Liu Zhao's note citing Zuo Duke Xi twenty-sixth year Du writes "Guixia."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye's Han treatise and Liu Zhao's Zuo gloss both read Guixia.

translations.literal: Nancheng originally wrote "Nanwucheng."
translations.idiomatic: An extra wu slipped into Nancheng in some prints.

sentences.zh: 考異：景獻羊皇后、惠羊皇后、羊祜傳、宋書羊欣、羊元保傳並云泰山南城人，宋、齊、隋志皆稱南城，惟晉志多一「武」字，殆因下文有「南武陽」而衍一「武」字。

translations.literal: Textual note: Empresses Jingxian and Hui of Yang, Yang Hu's biography, Songshu Yang Xin and Yang Yuanbao biographies all say people of Taishan Nancheng; Song, Qi, and Sui treatises all call it Nancheng; only Jin treatise adds one "wu" character, probably because below there is "Nanwuyang" and a redundant "wu" was interpolated.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies uniformly read Nancheng; the stray wu in Jin geography mirrors Nanwuyang below.

translations.literal: Note: Qian's view is correct; now deleted accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Editors drop the spurious wu following Qian Daxin.

translations.literal: Mou originally wrote "East Mou."
translations.idiomatic: Some copies prefixed East to Mou county.

translations.literal: Textual note: the character "east" is redundant.
translations.idiomatic: The east glyph is a dittography.

sentences.zh: 漢志上、《續漢志·三》泰山郡有牟縣，即春秋牟國，與東萊之東牟非一地。

translations.literal: Han Treatise I and Continuation Han Treatise III Taishan commandery has Mou County, i.e., Spring and Autumn Mou state; not the same place as East Mou in Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Han lists Mou in Taishan as the old Zhou polity, distinct from Donglai's East Mou.

sentences.zh: 羊祜傳詔以泰山之南武陽、牟、南城、梁父、平陽爲南城郡，是晉時已名牟縣也。

translations.literal: Yang Hu's biography edict used Taishan's Nanwuyang, Mou, Nancheng, Liangfu, Pingyang for Nancheng commandery, showing Jin already called it Mou County.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu's edict proves Jin already said Mou without the east prefix.

sentences.zh: 按：宋志一、《左傳》桓公十五年注「泰山牟縣」，均亦無「東」字，今據刪。

translations.literal: Note: Song Treatise I and Zuo Duke Huan fifteenth year commentary "Taishan Mou County" likewise lack the character "east"; now deleted accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Song treatise and Zuo Huan 15 agree on Mou without east; editors delete it.

sentences.zh: 長平馬校：縣已見前潁川郡，此誤複出。

translations.literal: Changping: Ma Coll.: county already seen above in Yingchuan commandery; wrongly duplicated here.
translations.idiomatic: Ma flags a duplicate Changping that belongs in Yingchuan, not here.

sentences.zh: 竺邑 《方校》：武陔傳，「沛國竹邑人」，此作「竺邑」，似誤。

translations.literal: Zhuyi: Fang Coll.: Wu Gai biography "man of Zhuyi in Pei," here writes "Zhuyi," seemingly error.
translations.idiomatic: Fang cites Wu Gai's bamboo-named hometown against the variant spelling used here.

sentences.zh: 斠注：魏志明紀、胡質傳引虞預晉書、宋書州郡志、水經睢水注引李奇說皆作「竹邑」。

translations.literal: Commentary note: Wei Records Emperor Ming, Hu Zhi biography citing Yu Yu's Jinshu, Song commandery treatise, Shuijing Sui water note citing Li Qi all write "Zhuyi."
translations.idiomatic: Parallel texts uniformly spell the county Zhuyi with the bamboo radical.

sentences.zh: 竺邑即竹邑，本漢縣，有竹邑侯張壽碑。

translations.literal: Zhuyi is Zhuyi, originally Han county; there is the Zhuyi marquis Zhang Shou stele.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuyi matches Han's bamboo-named county and an extant stele.

sentences.zh: 按：《漢志·上》、《續漢志·二》、《後漢書·明八王傳》、《吳志·薛綜傳》、《隋志·下》彭城郡符離下注並作「竹」。

translations.literal: Note: Han Treatise I, Continuation Han Treatise II, Later Han Treatise on the Eight Princes of Ming, Wu Records Xue Zong biography, Sui Treatise lower Pengyang commandery Fuli note all write "bamboo."
translations.idiomatic: Every canonical register keeps the bamboo graph.

sentences.zh: 蕃各本作「番」，今從宋本作「蕃」，與漢志下、《續漢志·二》合。

translations.literal: Fan: various editions write "fan"; now follow Song edition writing "Fan," matching Han Treatise lower and Continuation Han Treatise II.
translations.idiomatic: Song preserves Fan with the grass radical as Han and Xu do.

sentences.zh: 縣八十三「三」，各本作「二」，今從殿本作「三」，與實領縣數合。

translations.literal: Eighty-three counties: "three," various editions write "two"; now follow palace edition writing "three," matching the actual county count led.
translations.idiomatic: Palace prints say eighty-three counties to match the true tally.

sentences.zh: 易城漢志上、《續漢志·二》、後魏志上及後漢書劉虞傳並無「城」字。

translations.literal: Yicheng: Han Treatise I, Continuation Han Treatise II, Later Wei Treatise upper and Later Han Liu Yu biography all lack the character "city."
translations.idiomatic: Sources omit the extra cheng graph in Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 戶一萬八千一百「八千」，各本作「六千」，今從殿本作「八千」，與統計戶數相符。

translations.literal: Households eighteen thousand one hundred: "eight thousand," various editions write "six thousand"; now follow palace edition writing "eight thousand," matching the summarized household count.
translations.idiomatic: Palace edition restores eighteen thousand one hundred households to fit the census line.

sentences.zh: 陰氣雍閼也「陰」下原有「陽」字。

translations.literal: Yin qi blocked and shut: originally there was the character "yang" under "yin."
translations.idiomatic: A stray yang sat under yin in the Yizhou gloss.

sentences.zh: 斠注：類聚六、御覽一六四引太康地記均無「陽」字。

translations.literal: Commentary note: Classified Compendium six and Imperial Readings 164 citing Taikang land record both lack the character "yang."
translations.idiomatic: Early encyclopedia citations omit the yang insert.

translations.literal: Note: lacking the character "yang" is correct; now deleted accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Editors strike the erroneous yang.

sentences.zh: 始平郡泰始二年置「二」，各本作「三」，今從宋本作「二」，與宋志三合。

translations.literal: Shiping commandery established Taishi second year: "two," various editions write "three"; now follow Song edition writing "two," matching Song Treatise III.
translations.idiomatic: Song aligns Taishi two with the Shiping founding date.

sentences.zh: 徙都 疑此二字因涉下文「徙都長安」而誤衍。

translations.literal: Moved capital: suspect these two characters wrongly interpolated by touching the below "moved capital to Chang'an."
translations.idiomatic: Editors treat the stray "moved capital" pair as contamination from the next line.

sentences.zh: 李閏姚萇載記、魏書安定王燮傳皆作「李潤」。

translations.literal: Liwei: Yao Chang's annals and Wei Records Prince Ding of Anding biography all write "Lirun."
translations.idiomatic: Parallel texts read Lirun, not Liwei.

sentences.zh: 避文帝諱改也「文」，原誤作「景」，今改正。

translations.literal: Avoiding Wendi taboo change: "Wen" originally mistakenly wrote "Jing"; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: A Jing/Wen slip in the taboo note is fixed.

translations.literal: Ming'an: "ming" originally wrote "yi."
translations.idiomatic: Mingan was miswritten Yian in the blockhead.

sentences.zh: 《畢校》：應作「冥安」，《元和郡縣志》以縣界冥水爲名。

translations.literal: Bi Coll.: should be "Ming'an"; Yuanhe commandery county treatise takes the county border Ming River as name.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Yuan restores Mingan from the river name in Yuanhe treatise.

translations.literal: Note: Bi's view is correct; now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The edition adopts Mingan per Bi Yuan.

translations.literal: Same below.
translations.idiomatic: The same correction applies in parallel entries below.

sentences.zh: 深泉考異：「淵泉」作「深泉」，避唐諱。

translations.literal: Shenquan textual note: "Yuanquan" written "Shenquan," avoiding Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Shenquan masks Yuanquan under Tang editing.

sentences.zh: 張駿分武威武興西平張掖酒泉建康西海西郡湟河晉興廣武合十一郡爲涼州 原缺「西海」，「廣武」誤作「須武」，今據《後魏書·張駿傳》補改。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun split Wuwei, Wuxing, Xiping, Zhangye, Jiuquan, Jiankang, Xihai, Xijun, Huanghe, Jinxing, Guangwu—altogether eleven commanderies—as Liangzhou: originally lacked "Xihai," "Guangwu" mistakenly wrote "Xuwu"; now supplemented and corrected according to Later Wei Records Zhang Jun biography.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei Zhang Jun biography supplies Xihai and fixes Guangwu against a garbled Xuwu.

sentences.zh: 敦煌晉昌高昌西域都護戊己校尉玉門大護軍三郡三營爲沙州 原缺「高昌」，「戊己」誤作「張茂以」，今據《後魏書·張駿傳》增改。

translations.literal: Dunhuang, Jinchang, Gaochang, Western Regions protector, gengji colonel, Yumen grand protector—three commanderies and three camps—as Shazhou: originally lacked "Gaochang," "gengji" mistakenly wrote "Zhang Mao used"; now increased and corrected according to Later Wei Records Zhang Jun biography.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Wei Zhang Jun biography restores Gaochang and the gengji colonel line mangled in transmission.

translations.literal: "Jin again became Tianshui" "Jin" should be "Wei."
translations.idiomatic: The line should credit Wei, not Jin, with restoring Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 魏時有天水郡，見三國志姜維傳及注、楊阜傳、曹真傳、張既傳、閻溫傳。

translations.literal: Wei times had Tianshui commandery; see Three Kingdoms Jiang Wei biography and notes, Yang Fu biography, Cao Zhen biography, Zhang Ji biography, Yan Wen biography.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sources already list Tianshui before Jin.

sentences.zh: 及獻帝初平六年趙一清水經注釋三三：全祖望謂初平只四年，無六年，當作元年。

translations.literal: When it came to Emperor Xian Chuping sixth year: Zhao Yi Shuijing commentary gloss 33: Quan Zuwang says Chuping only had four years, no sixth year; should be first year.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Zuwang notes Chuping lacked a year six; the year label should be Chuping one.

sentences.zh: 縣四十四各本作「縣三十三」，今從殿本作「縣四十四」，與統計實數合。

translations.literal: Forty-four counties: various editions write "thirty-three counties"; now follow palace edition writing "forty-four counties," matching the actual statistical count.
translations.idiomatic: Palace edition lists forty-four counties to match the table.

sentences.zh: 蜀置 《畢校》：譙周《巴記》，建安六年劉璋分巴郡墊江以上爲巴西郡。

translations.literal: Shu established: Bi Coll.: Qiao Zhou Ba Ji says sixth year of Jian'an Liu Zhang split Ba commandery above Dianjiang as Baxi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou dates Baxi to Liu Zhang's Jian'an six split.

sentences.zh: 據此，則巴西郡劉璋時分置。

translations.literal: According to this, then Baxi commandery was separately established in Liu Zhang's time.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Baxi belongs to Liu Zhang's reorganization, not Shu Han alone.

sentences.zh: 魚復各本作「魚腹」，今從宋本作「魚復」。

translations.literal: Yufu: various editions write the name with the "fish-belly" graphs; now follow Song edition writing the "fish-repeat" graphs.
translations.idiomatic: Song preserves the standard spelling Yufu for the county, rejecting the belly-character variant.

sentences.zh: 漢志上、《續漢志·五》、華陽國志一、後漢書張堪傳、蜀志先主傳並作「魚復」。

translations.literal: Han Treatise I, Continuation Han Treatise V, Huayang Guo Zhi I, Later Han Zhang Kan biography, Shu Records First Ruler biography all write "Yufu."
translations.idiomatic: All standard histories spell the county Yufu.

sentences.zh: 初平元年劉璋分巴郡立永寧郡考異：劉焉以興平元年卒，子璋始爲益州牧，則初平元年璋尚未牧益州，「初平」當爲「興平」之訛。

translations.literal: Chuping first year Liu Zhang split Ba to establish Yongning commandery textual note: Liu Yan died first year of Xingping, his son Zhang then became shepherd of Yizhou, so in Chuping first year Zhang had not yet governed Yizhou; "Chuping" should be error for "Xingping."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang could not split Ba in Chuping one because he was not yet shepherd; Xingping is the intended era.

translations.literal: Tanzhi originally wrote "Zhi tan."
translations.idiomatic: The two syllables of Tanzhi were reversed in the manuscript.

sentences.zh: 斠注：兩漢志、華陽國志四並作「談指」。

translations.literal: Commentary note: Two Han treatises and Huayang Guo Zhi IV all write "Tanzhi."
translations.idiomatic: Han and Huayang sources agree on Tanzhi order.

sentences.zh: 按：漢書昭帝紀、前漢紀十六亦作「談指」。

translations.literal: Note: Han Emperor Zhao annals and Former Han Chronicle sixteen likewise write "Tanzhi."
translations.idiomatic: Western Han court annals confirm Tanzhi.

translations.literal: Now corrected by transposition.
translations.idiomatic: Editors transpose the graphs to Tanzhi.

translations.literal: Wuyin originally wrote "Wu jian."
translations.idiomatic: A sword graph intruded for the correct yin.

sentences.zh: 斠注：兩漢志、宋志、華陽國志四、水經溫水注皆作「毋歛」。

translations.literal: Commentary note: Two Han treatises, Song treatise, Huayang Guo Zhi IV, Shuijing Wen River note all write "Wuyin."
translations.idiomatic: Parallel texts uniformly read Wuyin.

translations.literal: Note: "jian" is mistaken character; now changed.
translations.idiomatic: The edition restores Wuyin.

sentences.zh: 毋掇漢志上「掇」作「棳」，師古曰其字從木。

translations.literal: Wuduo: Han Treatise I writes "duo" as "zhuo"; Shigu says its character follows wood.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu's Han treatise spells the county with the wood radical variant.

translations.literal: Shuijing Wen River note likewise writes "Wuzhuo."
translations.idiomatic: Li Daoyuan keeps the woody spelling in Shuijing.

translations.literal: Tanfeng: "tan," various editions write "duo."
translations.idiomatic: Some blocks miswrite Tanfeng's first character as duo.

sentences.zh: 宋本及音義作「鐔」，今從宋本。

translations.literal: Song edition and phonological glosses write "tan"; now follow Song edition.
translations.idiomatic: Song and fanqie agree on the metal radical tan.

sentences.zh: 與漢志上、《續漢志·五》、宋志四、華陽國志四、水經溫水注合。

translations.literal: Matches Han Treatise I, Continuation Han Treatise V, Song treatise IV, Huayang Guo Zhi IV, Shuijing Wen River note.
translations.idiomatic: The tan spelling matches every major gazetteer.

sentences.zh: 永嘉二年至夜郎二郡 王遜傳：「元帝加遜安南將軍，刺史如故。

translations.literal: Yongjia second year to Yelang two commanderies: Wang Xun biography: "Emperor Yuan added Xun as General Who Guards the South, inspector as before.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun's biography ties Yongjia-era splits to Yuan's promotion of Xun as southern general while he stayed inspector.

sentences.zh: 遜表請改分牂牁爲平夷郡，分建寧爲夜郎郡，改益州爲晉寧郡，事皆施行。

translations.literal: Xun submitted a memorial asking to split Zangke into Pingyi commandery, split Jianning into Yelang commandery, change Yizhou to Jinning commandery; matters were all implemented.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial carved Pingyi and Yelang from Zangke and Jianning and renamed Yizhou Jinning.

translations.literal: " This differs from this treatise.
translations.idiomatic: That sequence disagrees with the wording in this geography chapter.
